Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Elextensions ELEX WordPress HelpDesk & Customer Ticketing System elex-helpdesk-customer-support-ticket-system allows Object Injection.This issue affects ELEX WordPress HelpDesk & Customer Ticketing System: from n/a through 3.3.9.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Sarah Giles Dynamic User Directory dynamic-user-directory allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects Dynamic User Directory: from n/a through 2.4.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Sarah Giles Dynamic User Directory dynamic-user-directory allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Dynamic User Directory: from n/a through 2.4.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in CleverReach CleverReach® WP cleverreach-wp allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects CleverReach® WP: from n/a through 1.5.26.

Zohocorp ManageEngine M365 Manager Plus versions below 4818 is affected by an authenticated technician may exploit insufficient permission validation in the delegated administration interface to escalate privileges beyond their intended scope, which could result in remote code execution during administrative processing.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2 does not restrict the destination filename and extension, nor validate the fetched content type, when importing remote media, allowing an Administrator of a Multisite subsite to write and execute arbitrary PHP in the shared WordPress context despite not being a Network Administrator and being unable to install WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2 or edit files.

The Recipe Card Blocks Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'steps[].text' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.7.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Because wp_kses_post() preserves block-delimiter HTML comments verbatim on save, a Contributor can embed event-handler payloads inside the block's steps[].text attribute in a draft or pending post without the unfiltered_html capability, and the payload executes for any visitor — including privileged editors and administrators who preview or publish the post — as well as through the public print endpoint.

Dental practice sites hosted with iDentalSoft send a JSON response to any user who loads certain pages containing sensitive information, including OAuth credentials, password hashes, and PII. Fixed in iDentalSoft 14.0.3.

The Streamit WordPress plugin before 1.3.10 does not perform any authorization or nonce verification on one of its unauthenticated AJAX routes, which invokes an attacker-supplied PHP function with an attacker-supplied argument array, allowing unauthenticated attackers to call arbitrary functions (for example to create an administrator account), leading to privilege escalation and remote code execution.

The AutomatorWP Pro plugin for WordPress' webhook addon is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.4. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reset the password of any WordPress account, including administrators, resulting in full account takeover. This is only exploitable when an administrator has configured an automation pairing a Receive Webhook trigger — with an 'Is the user ID' field — to an Update-User action whose User ID field is left blank and whose Password field is mapped to the webhook password tag, which is a documented, supported plugin configuration.

Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 4.0, Soup Sieve repeatedly walks the same ancestors while matching descendant combinators, and each additional descendant combinator raises the polynomial degree of the work on deeply nested attacker-influenced HTML or XML. Applications using selectors such as section div div through select(), select_one(), or Beautiful Soup CSS APIs against untrusted documents can have a worker occupied for seconds or minutes, while trusted-only document processing is not affected. Selectors compiled with NOCACHE continue to use the old uncached behavior. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.

Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 3.0, the CSS_ESCAPES and IDENTIFIER regular-expression subpatterns can backtrack exponentially on runs of ambiguous digit escapes in an attribute-name or tag position of an otherwise valid selector. The failure occurs during selector compilation through soupsieve.compile() or Beautiful Soup select() before SELECTOR_LIMIT is applied, so an application that accepts untrusted selector strings can have a worker stalled by a short input. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.

pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, custom pl-do tools interpolated JSON arguments into a PostgreSQL DO block delimited by fixed dollar-quote tags. An argument containing $mcp_custom_tool$ could terminate the block and inject arbitrary SQL statements, while $mcp_args$ could inject procedural code into a plpgsql block. Because the statement used the simple query protocol, injected text could include additional statements and transaction control, bypassing read_only and accessing data or modifying resources available to the connecting role. The issue requires at least one pl-do custom tool; sql and pl-func tools pass arguments as bind parameters and are not affected by this injection mechanism. This issue is fixed in 1.1.0.

express-rate-limit is a basic rate-limiting middleware for Express. From 8.6.0 until 8.7.2, the built-in MemoryStore returns a Client whose mutable resetTime object is retained by middleware using skipFailedRequests or skipSuccessfulRequests. When a later request resets the client window, MemoryStore.resetClient mutates that same Date, so an earlier request that finishes or disconnects after the reset can pass the stale-window guard and decrement the current window's count. A client able to keep requests in flight across the boundary can obtain a bounded extra burst of up to one additional configured limit in the new window; the behavior does not increase the sustained rate. Stores that return a fresh Date are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 8.7.2.

Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. In 2.25.2, Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? treats a data URI mediatype containing the HTML5 named solidus reference / as malformed and falls back to the allowed text/plain, while a browser decodes the reference and interprets the same value as text/html. An application that validates a user-controlled URL with this helper and renders the approved value in href or another browser-interpreted URI attribute can allow cross-site scripting. Rails::HTML::Sanitizer.allowed_uri? re-exports the affected helper. Loofah's default sanitize() path is not affected because Nokogiri decodes the entity before URI validation. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

Loofah is a general library for manipulating and transforming HTML/XML documents and fragments, built on top of Nokogiri. Prior to 2.25.3, Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.scrub_css checks only the first parse of a style attribute, then rebuilds CSS with identifier escapes decoded so escaped parentheses, property names, comments, or quotes can become a live url() without a second safety check. An attacker can use list-style to make a viewer's browser request an attacker-chosen URL when content renders, or cursor to make the request on hover. The request can disclose the viewer's IP address, user agent, access timing, and access to internal-network hosts, but no script survives sanitization and the attacker cannot read the response. This issue is fixed in version 2.25.3.

'@hono/node-server allows running the Hono application on Node.js. Prior to 1.19.18 and from 2.0.0 until 2.1.6, the server passes a raw request-target containing a backslash in its path to the WHATWG URL parser, which treats the backslash as a path separator and resolves dot segments. A reverse proxy, load balancer, or web application firewall that preserves the backslash and applies path-based rules to the original request can therefore permit a request that the application normalizes to a blocked route. This lets an unauthenticated client reach route content that the upstream component was intended to deny, while Hono application access controls are unaffected because they operate on the normalized path. This issue is fixed in versions 1.19.18 and 2.1.6.

SiYuan from 3.6.0 before 3.8.9 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated publish visitors to bypass per-document passwords via regex search in getDoc. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/filetree/getDoc with queryMethod 3 and a broad regex to read protected body text returned in the unfiltered keywords field.

NocoDB from 0.300.0 before 2026.04.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to crash the server by triggering an unhandled promise rejection in MetaService metadata logging. Attackers can send a request leaving a lookup condition undefined, causing knex binding errors in the unawaited logHelper call that terminate the server process.

NocoDB before 2026.09.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the aggregated meta info route of utils.controller.ts that exposes instance-wide metadata to anonymous callers. Unauthenticated attackers can request the endpoint to enumerate bases, user counts, shared and password-protected view counts, webhook counts, and live per-base row counts, while repeated requests amplify database query load.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated base Viewers to obtain TLS client private keys by reading a base's data source. The source read handler masked only the connection password, letting attackers retrieve the decrypted private key, client certificate and CA to connect directly to the external database, bypassing NocoDB permissions.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator users to inject script by embedding markup in column or table titles. The Delete.vue confirmation dialog renders these titles through an unescaped innerHTML binding, executing script when a victim deletes an external-source table to steal session tokens from localStorage.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read cross-base row comments by supplying only model and row ids. Attackers with a Viewer or Creator role on an unrelated base can read private comments and author emails, or plant decoy tables and duplicate comment ids to spoof teammates' comments.

NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains a race condition vulnerability in users.service.ts that allows holders of a valid reset token to perform multiple password changes by sending concurrent reset requests. Attackers can exploit the window created by slow bcrypt hashing before the token is cleared to overwrite the owner's new password and lock them out.

NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in PromptWithFields.vue that renders unescaped field references from AI field prompts as HTML in a tooltip. Attackers with the Creator role or above can store markup in a prompt's field reference that executes when victims open the field configuration, stealing the localStorage session token to call authenticated APIs as the victim.

NocoDB from 2026.04.0 before 2026.08.0 contains an improper privilege management vulnerability in org-users.service.ts where updating a user's legacy organization role rewrites their default-workspace role. Revoked users can silently regain Creator-level read, write and schema modification access across all default-workspace bases using their existing session token.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that lets base-scoped API tokens act as account-wide credentials because the token's base_id is never stored or checked. Attackers holding a leaked token can read, write and delete records on every base the token owner belongs to, including bases joined later.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in PageLeavingWarning.vue that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute script by embedding an ASCII control character in the ncRedirectUrl scheme. Attackers can send a crafted link that bypasses the scheme check and reaches the anchor href or window.location, stealing the session token from localStorage for account takeover.

NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains a race condition vulnerability in oauth-token.service.ts that allows attackers to reuse a refresh token by presenting it concurrently during non-atomic rotation. Attackers holding a captured refresh token can race the legitimate client to obtain their own access and refresh tokens, retaining scoped access without triggering reuse detection.

NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in base-integrations.service.ts that allows authenticated base members to read private integration configurations by omitting a query flag. Attackers can request another user's private integration without the configuration flag, bypassing the ownership check to obtain stored connection credentials.

NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in base-user.cte.utils.ts, which concatenates base members' email addresses into the SQL text of queries resolving user, created-by or last-modified-by fields. Registered users can set an email with a quoted local part containing a single quote to execute arbitrary SQL, exposing user records, API tokens and data-source credentials.

Grav Login plugin before 3.11.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers with an account password to skip two-factor verification when the global twofa_enabled setting is off. Attackers can sign in through the /login form, remember-me cookie, or magic link to obtain a session the API plugin accepts, gaining full account permissions including super-admin control.

NLTK from 3.10.0 before 3.10.4 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability in BllipParser that allows attackers to open files outside NLTK data roots by supplying unvalidated model paths. Attackers controlling parser_model, reranker_features, reranker_weights, or from_unified_model_dir() input can make the bllipparser C extension read sensitive files or block on FIFOs and devices.

NLTK before 3.10.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability in Tree.chomsky_normal_form that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU through quadratic-time right-factor binarization using list.pop(0). Attackers can supply a wide flat treebank tree parsed by Tree.fromstring to force tens of seconds of single-threaded CPU consumption, blocking the processing thread.

NLTK before 3.10.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the CCG lexicon parser fromstring that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying wide inputs. Attackers can submit lexicon text with long flat bracket bodies or operator chains, triggering quadratic string re-slicing in matchBrackets and augParseCategory that blocks worker threads.

NLTK from 3.9.4 before 3.10.4 contains a symlink following vulnerability in nltk.sem.chat80.sql_query() that bypasses the pathsec data-root sandbox containment check. Attackers who can write into a trusted NLTK data root can plant a symbolic link to read SQLite databases outside the sandbox.

NLTK before 3.10.4 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in SteppingRecursiveDescentParser.parse() that lacks any max_time deadline or step limit. Attackers influencing the grammar can supply an ambiguous self-embedding grammar and short token input to force unbounded top-down search, pinning CPU cores and exhausting worker pools.

EspoCRM before 9.3.11 and 10.x before 10.0.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged users to upload crafted SVG images that submit authenticated POST requests to arbitrary backend endpoints. Attackers can trick an administrator into opening the SVG in a separate browser tab and clicking it, performing administrator actions such as elevating the attacker's account to administrator.

Nezha Dashboard before 2.6.0 contains multiple authorization, tenant isolation, and resource exhaustion vulnerabilities that allow members or unauthenticated attackers to abuse NAT, DDNS, OAuth, cron, and server transfer features. Attackers can claim undeclared Dashboard hostnames to capture login bodies, hijack DDNS profiles, create executable schedules without exec scope, or exhaust memory via buffered NAT requests.

OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated callers to obtain OIDC ID tokens by abusing public clients with client_credentials enabled. Attackers who know a public client's client_id can request tokens from the identity/oidc/provider/<name>/token endpoint to impersonate the client without any secret.

OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.x before 2.7.2 does not neutralize wildcard characters in SSH certificate principals rendered from unvalidated external token metadata via identity templates in the SSH secrets engine. Attackers controlling that metadata, typically through a compromised identity provider, can inject '*' to obtain SSH certificates valid for multiple hosts or users.

Frappe HRMS 15.0.0 before 15.64.6 and 16.0.0 before 16.20.1 does not check access to each employee on endpoints that create records in bulk for a list of employees. An authenticated user with create permission on the affected record type, such as HR User, can create records for employees outside their user-permission scope, including other companies' employees.

Frappe HRMS 16.14.0 before 16.20.1 sends product usage events on certain HR transactions without checking the site's telemetry setting, and some events include more detail than needed. During normal use, with no user action, values such as leave type names, claimed amounts and appraisal scores are transmitted even when telemetry is disabled.

REDAXO before 5.21.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows editors without the version[live_version] permission to modify live article versions by bypassing working version enforcement. Authenticated editors can add, edit, delete, toggle, or reorder live slices via content/functions, slice ids, content_slice_status, content_move_slice, history restore, or content_copy, bypassing approval workflows.

Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows authenticated users with stacks:create permission to read sensitive files by supplying an arbitrary composePath during stack adoption. Attackers can adopt a stack pointing to the encryption key, SQLite database, or /proc/self/environ and read it via the compose endpoint to obtain all stored credentials.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an unsanitized deserialization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to control patient-matching criteria by supplying a crafted serialized key parameter. Attackers can send serialized arrays to interface/orders/patient_match_dialog.php to enumerate patients or force matches that associate lab orders with the wrong patient.

Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to perform admin state-changing actions because checkCsrf() in admin/controller/base.php only validates tokens for POST requests. Attackers can lure a logged-in admin into loading a forged cross-site GET request to delete admin/user accounts, sites, orders, and menus or change comment status.

Replying to a code review comment accepted a review ID that belongs to a different pull request, through the web form, the API and incoming mail replies. A signed-in user could reply on a pull request they can access with the ID of a review in a repository they cannot read, and the new comment was attached to that review and received the diff context of the commented lines. Replies are now only accepted for a review of the same pull request, and for a pending review only from its author.

'@hono/node-server allows running the Hono application on Node.js. From 2.0.0 until 2.1.6, the WebSocket upgrade handler waits for the Hono application to finish asynchronous middleware or handler work without first attaching an error listener to the socket. If an unauthenticated client resets the TCP connection during that window, the socket emits an unhandled ECONNRESET error and terminates the Node.js process. If a global uncaughtException handler suppresses termination, the pending upgrade waiter is not released and repeated requests can grow the heap. This affects applications that enable WebSocket support and perform asynchronous work on the upgrade path. This issue is fixed in version 2.1.6.

basic-ftp is an FTP client for Node.js. Prior to 6.2.3, FTPContext.send() throws when a command contains carriage return, line feed, or NUL characters, but calls made from response handlers execute synchronously inside the control socket's data event without an exception boundary. In Client.login(), an attacker-influenced password reaches the PASS command after a server sends a 331 response, and in a resumed download an attacker-influenced remote path reaches the RETR command after a 350 response to REST. The resulting exception does not reject client.access() or downloadTo(), escapes ordinary promise error handling, and terminates the Node.js process, while the validation guard still prevents command injection. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.3.

Tornado is a Python web framework and asynchronous networking library. In versions through 6.6.0, applications using  tornado.web.RedirectHandler  with URL templates that allow attacker-controlled substitutions to influence the destination can be vulnerable to an open redirect using three or more leading slashes. Differences between Python’s URL parsing and browser URL interpretation allow a crafted destination to redirect a user to an attacker-controlled host. The remediation for CVE-2026-116578 in version 6.6.0 did not fully address this case. This issue is fixed in version 6.6.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. From 2.0.0 until 2.9.1, the pure-Ruby Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode implementation decodes invalid Punycode A-labels instead of returning them unchanged. Labels that decode to ASCII text or fail to convert back to the same A-label can therefore make Addressable::URI#display_uri show a trusted-looking host while host, normalized_host, and the connection target retain the attacker-controlled encoded host. A trusted-name comparison using Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode output can also treat two different hosts as the same without displaying the URI. The native libidn implementation, to_ascii, and normalized_host are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. From 2.0.0 until 2.9.1, Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode can decode Punycode labels that contain bidirectional controls, zero-width characters, control characters, or other default-ignorable format characters. Addressable::URI#display_uri can consequently show a reordered or visually indistinguishable hostname even though host, normalized_host, and network connections use the original encoded hostname. The pure-Ruby backend accepts the full prohibited set, while the native libidn backend is affected from 2.5.2 for characters added after Unicode 3.2. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. From 2.3.0 until 2.9.1, URI template expressions using the explode modifier with the slash, dot, semicolon, question-mark, or ampersand operators generate ambiguous regular expressions. When Template#match or Template#extract processes an attacker-controlled URI beginning with the operator's leading character, optional member separators allow catastrophic backtracking and denial of service on MRI Ruby before 3.2 and JRuby. Addressable 2.9.0 incompletely remediated the earlier template issue because its tests did not reach these operator-prefixed paths. URI parsing and Template#expand are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. Prior to 2.9.1, Addressable::URI.normalize_path repeatedly scans and rewrites paths while removing only one nested dot segment per pass, producing quadratic work. URI#normalize, URI#normalized_path, URI#join, URI#==, and URI#=== inherit the behavior, so processing a sufficiently long attacker-controlled URI can consume a worker thread and cause denial of service on every Ruby implementation. URI.parse alone and code that never normalizes, compares, or joins untrusted URIs are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. From 2.3.0 until 2.9.1, URI templates with several variables in one expression or several adjacent expressions generate ambiguous regular expressions. Affected forms include multi-variable expressions using operators other than plus and number sign, large plus or number-sign expressions, and adjacent single-variable expressions. Template#match or Template#extract can backtrack polynomially or exponentially on attacker-controlled URIs, causing denial of service on MRI Ruby before 3.2 and JRuby, with the large plus and number-sign form also affecting MRI Ruby 3.2 and TruffleRuby 40.0. URI parsing and Template#expand are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. From 2.3.0 until 2.9.1, URI template expressions containing several exploded variables generate ambiguous regular expressions that can divide a run of members among the variables in polynomially many ways. Template#match or Template#extract processing of an attacker-controlled URI can therefore consume a thread and cause denial of service. The flaw affects MRI Ruby before 3.2 and JRuby, TruffleRuby 40.0, and plus or number-sign expressions on MRI Ruby 3.2. MRI Ruby 3.3 and later, URI parsing, and Template#expand are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Addressable is an alternative implementation to the URI implementation that is part of Ruby's standard library. From 2.2.5 until 2.9.1, Addressable::URI.normalize_path can resolve a path containing leading parent segments and later parent segments to a different path than an RFC 3986 resolver. URI#normalize, URI#join, URI#==, and URI#=== inherit the result. An application that authorizes the Addressable-normalized path but sends the original URI to another resolver can allow access outside the intended path allowlist. Applications that use the same normalized value for authorization and the request, or reject parent segments, are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.1.

Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Prior to 4.13.16, csrf() limits origin validation to the content types normally sent by HTML forms and therefore does not validate text/ping requests generated by Chromium hyperlink auditing. Chrome and Edge can send a cross-origin credentialed POST without a CORS preflight through an <a ping> action, and the middleware then skips both Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks. The fixed request body limits exploitation to state-changing endpoints whose effect is selected by the path or query string and does not depend on submitted body data. The user's cookie must accompany the request, which generally requires a same-site origin or a cookie configured with SameSite=None, and Firefox does not send hyperlink-auditing pings by default. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.

Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. From 4.1.4 until 4.13.16, RegExpRouter can omit wildcard middleware in three version-specific cases: since 4.13.0, middleware using the explicit default parameter pattern in /api/:tenant{[^/]+}/admin/* is not applied to a route written as /api/:tenant/admin/:id; since 4.1.4, middleware on /admin/* is not applied to a route registered as /admin* for paths under /admin/; and since 4.4.0, a request path containing an encoded line terminator can reach the not-found handler without wildcard middleware. The default SmartRouter selects RegExpRouter for most applications, and the router's registration-time coverage calculation treated the first two matching pattern pairs as different while its compiled wildcard did not match line terminators in the third case. An unauthenticated client can reach a route handler or the not-found handler without authentication or authorization middleware registered on the wildcard path. TrieRouter, LinearRouter, and PatternRouter apply the middleware in the three described cases. This issue is fixed in version 4.13.16.

Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to 7.4.5, Astro rendered a string used as a dynamic element name as raw HTML after applying an incomplete character filter. A / in the string could make an HTML parser treat the remainder as attributes, allowing untrusted element-name input to inject event-handler markup. The .astro dynamic-tag renderer, JSX renderer, and MDX renderer were affected, and exploitation required an application to use request-controlled or stored untrusted data as all or part of an element name. This issue is fixed in version 7.4.5.

Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.7.3 until 9.1.2, the @astrojs/svelte renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. Request-controlled slot names containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Svelte component using a client:* directive and dynamic rendering of the attacker-chosen slot; components that did not render that slot emitted only Astro's escaped fallback content. Both server rendering and client-side hydration used the unsafe slot name. This issue is fixed in version 9.1.2.

MessagePack for Ruby is an implementation of the MessagePack binary serialization format. Prior to 1.8.7, the Java-platform msgpack gem for JRuby allocated arrays and byte buffers directly from attacker-controlled array32, str32, and bin32 declared sizes before confirming that corresponding elements or bytes were available. A short MessagePack header could therefore trigger a very large allocation or sustained heap growth when an application decoded untrusted input through MessagePack.unpack or MessagePack::Unpacker, potentially exhausting the shared JVM heap. map32 and declared counts at or above 2^31 did not use the affected allocation behavior. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.7.

Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in Admin_Auth_TokenSQL::update(), which interpolates admin_auth_token array keys into an INSERT column list without a column whitelist or backtick escaping. Authenticated admin-panel users can submit backtick-containing keys to the admin/auth-token save action to inject comments and column identifiers into the SQL statement.

Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-41934 that allows authenticated editor or site_admin users to write server-side templates by bypassing save restrictions. Attackers can upload or rename .tpl files via editor/code upload and rename actions, or evade isExecutableFile checks in save(), to inject PHP code into templates.

Vvveb through 1.0.8.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows low-privilege vendors to rename, delete, or overwrite other vendors' digital-asset files in the shared storage/digital_assets directory. Attackers can send rename, delete, or upload requests to product/digital-asset with another vendor's filename to break downloads or substitute malicious content.

Vvveb 1.0.8.4 through 1.0.8.6 contains an incomplete authorization fix that allows low-privilege authors and vendors to access other users' records by bypassing admin_id owner scoping. Attackers can supply filter[admin_id] to list drafts, invoke duplicate() on posts or products, or enumerate every vendor's digital-asset metadata.

Vvveb 1.0.8.6 contains an incomplete server-side request forgery fix that allows authenticated admin users to bypass DNS pinning by requesting non-443 URLs. Attackers can supply a rebinding hostname to the editor oEmbedProxy url parameter to read loopback services, internal panels, and cloud metadata credentials.

Vvveb before 1.0.9.0 contains a denylist bypass in system/traits/media.php where '.phar' is misconfigured with a leading dot, allowing authenticated administrators to upload .phar PHP files. Attackers can upload a GIF magic-byte polyglot webshell bypassing binary inspection and execute arbitrary OS commands as the web-server user.

n8n before 1.123.89, 2.x before 2.45.5, 2.46.x before 2.46.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains a NoSQL injection vulnerability in the MongoDB node's Update and Find And Replace operations due to insufficient validation of the update key value taken from incoming items. Attackers who can supply untrusted input, such as a webhook body, to a workflow using these operations can make the node match and overwrite unintended documents or insert new documents in the MongoDB database.

n8n before 1.123.89, 2.x before 2.45.5, 2.46.x before 2.46.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 bundles a GraphicsMagick version with known vulnerabilities in its official Docker image, which the Edit Image node uses to process images. Attackers who can supply crafted untrusted images to an Edit Image workflow, such as one fed by a Webhook node, can execute code on the n8n instance.

n8n before 2.46.1 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows authenticated members to read server files by supplying absolute paths to the Browser Use browser_upload tool. Attackers with a connected remote browser session can have Playwright read files such as instance configuration from the n8n server and retrieve their contents from the page.

n8n before 2.46.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that forwards Authorization headers and basic auth credentials on cross-origin redirects because sendCredentialsOnCrossOriginRedirect defaults to true. Attackers controlling a redirect target or an expression-fed URL in credential-using nodes can capture stored workflow credentials sent to their endpoint.

n8n before 1.123.89 contains an insufficient isolation vulnerability in workflow expression evaluation that allows authenticated users to escape the sandbox. Attackers with permission to create or modify workflows can craft expressions referencing unexpected JavaScript properties to execute arbitrary code on the n8n host.

Parse Server from 9.10.6-alpha.1 before 9.10.8-alpha.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients with write but not read access to learn whether fields are stored on MongoDB. Attackers can send updates with dot notation operations on top-level fields and observe internal server errors versus success responses to infer field existence.

vLLM from 0.14.0rc1 before 0.31.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in sanitize_message() whose lowercase-only regex fails to scrub uppercase PIL image addresses. Unauthenticated attackers can send a crafted PNG to endpoints such as /tokenize, triggering HF-processor errors that leak live server heap addresses useful for ASLR bypass.

vLLM from 0.24.0 before 0.31.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the MiniMax M3 VL video processor, which accepts request-level min_pixels without range or min_pixels <= max_pixels validation. Its video-wide pixel budget is enforced only when max_long_side_pixel is set, and that value defaults to None. API clients can supply a large min_pixels via mm_processor_kwargs to enlarge every decoded frame, causing excessive CPU and host-memory consumption that may disrupt workers or the service.

vLLM from 0.19.0 before 0.31.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows inference clients to bypass the server frame limit by setting media_io_kwargs.video.num_frames in chat completion requests. Attackers can supply num_frames=-1 or a large value with many base64 JPEG frames, forcing VideoMediaIO to decode all frames and np.stack them, causing memory exhaustion.

Password Pusher from 1.49.0 before 2.17.0 contains an IP spoofing vulnerability that allows remote clients to forge the recorded request IP via unanchored trusted-proxy regular expressions. Clients in 110.0.0.0/8 or 210.0.0.0/8, or connecting directly, can supply X-Forwarded-For values to falsify audit log entries and shift password generator rate limits.

Coder 2.26.0 before 2.29.24, 2.30.0 before 2.34.16, 2.35.0 before 2.36.11, 2.37.0 before 2.37.8, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 contains an improper authorization flaw in the external agent credentials endpoint, which returns the workspace agent token to users with only workspace read access rather than ssh permission. Authenticated users with roles such as Template Admin or Organization Admin can use the token to read the owner's private Git SSH key and Git provider OAuth tokens, and impersonate the agent to receive the owner's sessions.

Coder 2.28.0 before 2.29.24, 2.30.0 before 2.34.16, 2.35.0 before 2.36.11, 2.37.0 before 2.37.8, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 does not restrict new API keys to the creating token's scopes, allow list, or expiry. A scoped API key or OAuth2 token holding key-creation permission can call POST /api/v2/users/{user}/keys/tokens to mint longer-lived coder:all keys, gaining the user's full privileges.

Wasmtime before 36.0.20, 37.0.0 before 48.0.8, 49.0.0 before 49.0.5, and 50.0.0 before 50.0.1 allocates untracked host memory when a component receives a borrow of a resource it defines itself, bypassing the per-store handle limit. A malicious guest component can repeatedly transfer such borrowed resources to consume arbitrary host memory, causing denial of service.

Wasmtime 47.0.0 before 48.0.8, 49.0.0 before 49.0.5, and 50.0.0 before 50.0.1 contains an insufficient type-check in the TypedFunc embedder API for I31, Option<I31>, and Option<NoneRef> parameter or result types, reaching an unreachable!() path. A malicious guest module exporting a function that uses another anyref-hierarchy type can panic the host embedding, causing denial of service.

Frappe HRMS 16.0.0 before 16.50.0 lacks authorization checks on certain HR workflow endpoints, letting authenticated users access records they are not permitted to view. Any logged-in user, including one with only the Employee role, can read candidate record details and employee email addresses, and cause emails to be sent to employees.

Frappe HRMS 15.0.0 before 15.64.1 and 16.0.0 before 16.19.0 lacks a write permission check on a bulk record processing action, allowing users with only read access to the related setup record to modify data. Authenticated users with the default Employee role can run the action to create and submit records for every covered employee.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Patient Validation module that allows any authenticated user to retrieve patient demographic records. Attackers can send direct requests with wildcard mf_lname or empty mf_ parameters to the patientvalidation endpoint to enumerate the entire patient_data table.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in patient_tracker_status.php that allows low-privilege authenticated users to modify other patients' tracker entries by supplying arbitrary tracker_id values. Attackers can post statustype and roomnum parameters with a valid CSRF token to alter patient-flow status, room assignments, and linked calendar appointment state.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the esign_form_submit handler of library/ESign/Form/Controller.php that verifies only the caller's password, not access to the patient, encounter, or form type. Authenticated core users can supply arbitrary formId, formDir, and encounterId values to sign and lock any patient's clinical form, creating unauthorized approval records and blocking normal editing.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the FaxSMS module's utility.php that allows read-only demographics users to create patient charts. Attackers can submit the form_create request with chosen identity fields to create fictitious or duplicate patients with employer, history, and insurance records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in four ZIP upload paths that read uncompressed entries into memory without size or ratio checks. Authenticated billing or Carecoordination users can upload highly compressed ZIP archives to exhaust PHP memory and worker pools, making OpenEMR unavailable.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with admin/superbill write permission to inject HTML into SNOMED code descriptions via superbill_custom_full.php. When a clinician selects the malicious code, the Functional and Cognitive Status form or fee-sheet forms assign it to innerHTML, executing JavaScript in the clinician's session to read patient data and perform actions.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a session expiration vulnerability that prevents automatic logoff because the Eye Exam form's read-only poll omits skip_timeout_reset. Attackers with physical access to an unattended workstation can use the still-active session to view patient health information, since update_READONLY() resets the idle timer every 15 seconds.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated billing users to store attacker-controlled PHP by uploading a malformed ERA file to era_payments.php. Attackers with a database-write primitive such as SQL injection can register a background_services row whose require_once loads the stored .edi file, executing PHP as the web-server user.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a second-order sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Carecoordination users to store malicious C-CDA field identifiers through the savedata action. Attackers can inject SQL into the IN clause built by fetchFormValues() during C-CDA generation to extract password hashes, portal reset values, and patient records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in interface/orders/list_reports.php that allows read-only users to transmit lab orders because the patients/med check ignores write permission. Authenticated attackers can submit form_xmit with arbitrary procedure order IDs to send HL7 orders containing SSNs, insurance, and diagnoses to laboratories and mark them transmitted.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in interface/orders/order_manifest.php, which checks patients/med without requiring write access or applying patient squad restrictions. Users with only patients/med view permission can request any order ID to read squad-restricted patient data and submit bn_save and form_omit parameters, without a CSRF token, to set do_not_send flags that suppress ordered lab procedures.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth2 clients to use unregistered grant types because oauth_clients.grant_types is never enforced. Attackers can request tokens with grant_type=password to bypass the user consent screen, and disabled clients can redeem authorization codes using JWT client assertions.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ccdaservice/ccda_gateway.php that fails to enforce the patients/pat_rep permission, accepting any authenticated core session. Authenticated users without patient-report permission can request the report_ccd_view action to retrieve the selected patient's C-CDA clinical summary, including diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, and identifiers.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization flaw in the Care Coordination CCDA and CCR import controllers, which move a document named by the document_id parameter into the import category without checking access to the source document. Authenticated non-administrators with Care Coordination access can recategorize protected patient documents and then download them through normal ACL-checked retrieval.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in dynamic_finder_ajax.php that allows authenticated users without patients/demo permission to query patient demographics. Attackers can supply arbitrary patient_data columns via the sColumns parameter to enumerate names, dates of birth, contact details, and Social Security numbers across the practice.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Ensora eRx integration that allows authenticated staff without patients/rx permission to access prescription data by directly requesting eRx.php. Attackers can expose selected patients' demographic, medication, and allergy data in the vendor XML and trigger eRx synchronization state changes.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in trusted-messages-ajax.php that allows any authenticated core user to send Direct messages without the patients/notes permission. Attackers with zero-ACL accounts can submit chosen recipients and message bodies sent via the clinic's phiMail credentials, impersonating the clinic to deliver fraudulent clinical communications.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users lacking nationnotes/nn_configure to modify shared Nation Notes templates by calling mutation endpoints directly. Attackers can send requests to ajax_code.php or add_context.php, which lack ACL and CSRF checks, to tamper with clinical-note templates and assignments.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows portal patients to run JavaScript in staff sessions by injecting javascript: URLs into document template_data. Attackers can submit an encounterForm value rendered unsanitized into an iframe src by DocumentTemplateRender, letting the script read PHI and CSRF tokens and call staff or admin endpoints.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in diagnosis_full.php that allows authenticated users to delete or clear any billing record by ID. Attackers can supply a target billing ID in the id parameter with delete or clear mode to deactivate other patients' charges and corrupt financial records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains multiple missing authorization and SQL injection defects across report, portal, transaction, and immunization components. Low-privileged Front Office clerks can chain these to read arbitrary database tables including users_secure hashes, hijack patient portal identities, and forge approved clinical records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Fee Sheet notecodes field, which is escaped with the wrong context. Attackers with clinician access can inject a payload that breaks out of the single-quoted value attribute and executes in higher-privileged users' browsers.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a persistent SQL injection vulnerability in SLEOB::slInvoiceNumber(), where the CLP01 claim control number from uploaded X12 835 ERA files is concatenated unescaped into a query. Attackers with billing write access can upload a crafted .edi file via sl_eob_search.php that is stored on the server and re-executes a time-based payload whenever it is reprocessed through sl_eob_process.php, extracting patient health information.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in library/ajax/user_settings.php that lets any authenticated user persist arbitrary global configuration overrides. Attackers can POST global:-prefixed keys to re-point external service hosts like CouchDB, eRx, phiMail, or SMTP to attacker-controlled servers, exfiltrating system credentials and patient PHI.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in PatientPortalPDFDocumentCreator::createPdfObject() that allows authenticated patients to make the server issue HTTP GET requests. Attackers can submit img src, inline style url(), or reinserted unpurified style blocks via the content parameter of portal/lib/doc_lib.php to probe internal ports and cloud metadata endpoints.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the patient portal api/onsiteactivityviews endpoint that allows any authenticated staff user to inject SQL through unquoted Id_BitwiseAnd Criteria values. Attackers can close the bitwise parenthesis and append OR or UNION SELECT clauses to read patient PHI, staff password hashes, MySQL authentication strings, and API tokens.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated low-privilege user to access reports, dated reminders, and batch reminder endpoints lacking AclMain::aclCheckCore() checks. Attackers can request patient_list.php, amc_full_report.php, dated_reminders_add.php, or batch_reminders.php directly to export patient PHI, send unauthorized reminders, and trigger batch reminder processing.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in several custom/ scripts that rely only on session authentication and never call AclMain::aclCheckCore(). Any authenticated low-privilege user can request export_labworks.php, chart_tracker.php, or export_registry_xml.php to disclose patient SSN, DOB, and insurance data or provider NPI/tax IDs, and forge chart-tracker records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ccdaservice/ccda_gateway.php that allows any authenticated low-privilege staff user to retrieve other patients' C-CDA documents. Attackers can request the view or dl action with sequential pid values and their own CSRF token to enumerate and exfiltrate medications, problems, allergies, and immunizations.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains OAuth scope canonicalization and containment flaws that allow unauthenticated attackers to obtain unapproved system-level FHIR access. Attackers can register a colon-form system:Patient.read client that bypasses approval, then request unregistered system/Patient.write scope to read, modify, and create Patient records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Application module's auto-suggest endpoint, which echoes the searchMode POST parameter unencoded into a single-quoted onClick attribute. Attackers can induce an authenticated user to submit a single-quote payload to application/index/search, executing arbitrary JavaScript in that user's session to steal session cookies or disclose patient data.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Eye Exam (eye_mag) module that allows administrators to inject JavaScript through unencoded Eye_defaults list option titles. Attackers can store a crafted title via edit_list.php that breaks out of a jQuery string in eye_base.php, executing script in any authenticated user's session when they click Defaults.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability in CcrTable::insertApprovedData() that allows authenticated users to inject SQL through request parameter names used as column names. Attackers can send crafted patient_data-*-sel parameters to the revandapprove route, lacking ACL and CSRF checks, to copy password hashes into patient fields or corrupt records.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in era_payments.php and sl_eob_search.php that allows authenticated billing users to write files outside the ERA directory. Attackers can embed traversal sequences in the GS04 element of an uploaded X12 835 file to overwrite .edi or .835 files with attacker-controlled content anywhere writable by the web server.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated report users to manipulate queries by supplying a crafted form_facility value to interface/reports/ippf_statistics.php. Attackers can close the string literal in the facility_id WHERE clause and use boolean or time-based payloads to read sensitive database contents.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in printed_fee_sheet.php that allows authenticated portal patients to inject script by setting unescaped appointment comments (pc_hometext). Attackers can submit HTML payloads via the form_comments field in add_edit_event_user.php that execute when staff open the patient's fee sheet, acting within the staff session.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in ObservationController::deleteAction that allows attackers to delete observation form records without a CSRF token. Attackers can lure a logged-in clinician to a page issuing a GET to delete.php with guessed id values, soft-deleting observations in the victim's open encounter.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in portal/import_template.php, where several portal document template modes lack admin/forms ACL and CSRF checks. Any authenticated staff user can send mode=save_profiles to delete all template profile assignments, use other unguarded modes to push templates to patients or change categories, and read template bodies via mode=get or getPdf.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to override system-wide global configuration values by storing global-prefixed keys through library/ajax/user_settings.php. Attackers can submit lab or target parameters with global: prefixed setting names to disable audit logging, weaken password policies, or alter security-sensitive settings persistently for their sessions.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the patient portal OnsiteDocument.Query endpoint, where mass-assigned _BitwiseAnd criteria parameters are placed unquoted into SQL with only quote-character escaping. Authenticated portal patients can inject SQL outside their per-patient scope to read the entire database, including other patients' demographics and users_secure password hashes.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a second-order SQL injection vulnerability in the IPPF contraceptive issue feature because issue_ippf_con_save concatenates layout_options field_id values into a REPLACE INTO query as column names. Authenticated administrators can add a malicious field_id via edit_layout.php, then trigger issue_ippf_con_save through add_edit_issue.php to execute arbitrary SQL.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains active debug code in interface/fax/fax_view.php that executes passthru("groups") and discloses the web server's Unix group memberships. Authenticated attackers with fax module access can supply a nonexistent jid value to reveal groups such as adm or shadow, aiding privilege escalation planning.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored SQL injection vulnerability in getByPatientDemographics() where layout_options field_id values are concatenated into the patient search WHERE clause. Attackers with Layout Editor access can plant a malicious field_id, allowing any authenticated low-privilege user to exfiltrate data from patient_data and users_secure tables.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a second-order sql injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to store malicious SQL via library/ajax/addlistitem.php. Attackers can persist a SQL fragment in the recent_patient_columns option_id value, which dynamic_finder.php concatenates into a SELECT query and executes as SQL.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged patient portal users to inject JavaScript via the tableArgs field of the onsiteportalactivity API. Attackers can store a payload with spaces that breaks out of an unquoted data-delete-id attribute, executing script when providers click the delete button on the audit review page.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2, WP Ultimate CSV Importer Pro WordPress plugin before 9.0.7 do not protect the files created by their single post export feature, writing them to a publicly accessible location under a predictable name, allowing unauthenticated attackers to download the content and custom fields of any exported post, including non-public content.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.3 does not escape values from imported files before using them in SQL queries when importing LifterLMS content, allowing high privilege users such as admin, including the administrator of a single site on a multisite network, to perform SQL injection attacks.

A link-following flaw was found in the authorized_key module of the ansible.posix collection, residual to the fix for CVE-2026-11837. That fix guards only the final path component (os.chown with follow_symlinks=False and O_NOFOLLOW in _safe_open_write()). When an unprivileged local user replaces their ~/.ssh directory with a symlink to a directory they do not own, and an operator subsequently runs the authorized_key task as root (a common provisioning pattern), the module resolves its path operations through the symlink: atomic_move() writes the temporary file in the symlink target and renames it to <target>/authorized_keys, creating or overwriting a file in the attacker-chosen directory, and os.chmod(sshdir, 0o700) follows the symlink and changes the target directory's permissions. The written file is chowned to the unprivileged user, so this is not a privilege escalation, but it allows an attacker to create or overwrite files (for example in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/, which APT reads regardless of file ownership) to cause integrity and availability impacts.

The Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 was distributed with a hidden update mechanism that fetched Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 updates from its author's own server instead of WordPress.org, which was used to push a backdoored build to sites, allowing the attacker controlling that server to inject arbitrary content into pages and to deliver arbitrary code to affected sites.

Version 5.2.1, as published on WordPress.org, bundled the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker library (updater/ directory) configured to poll https://anadnet.com/updates/?action=get_metadata&slug=quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4. In March 2021 that server delivered a modified 5.2.3 build, different from the 5.2.3 later published on WordPress.org, which kept the update channel and added a the_content filter that, for logged-out visitors on single posts and pages, fetched content from https://w.anadnet.com/bro/3/ (passing the site host, request URI and visitor User-Agent) and prepended the response to the post (observed serving SEO spam links to search engine crawlers). Because the version string matched a later WordPress.org release, affected sites were not offered a clean update until 5.2.4.

Indicators of compromise:
- Outbound requests to anadnet.com or w.anadnet.com
- An updater/ directory (Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker, Puc v4p10) inside wp-content/Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/
- The strings filter_the_content_in_the_main_loop, ppr_pro, QQQEND or w.anadnet.com in page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php
- page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php with MD5 ad717da18cf8a2b69899c0d7dafee05a (tampered 5.2.3)

Remediation: remove the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 (it has been closed on WordPress.org), or at minimum reinstall the clean 5.2.4 from WordPress.org, delete any leftover updater/ directory, verify the files with "wp Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 verify-checksums quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4", clear the opcode cache, and treat any site that ran the tampered build as potentially compromised.

A vulnerability was detected in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.0.2. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file .kimi-code/local.toml of the component WorkspaceDirsService. Performing a manipulation of the argument additional_dir results in reliance on untrusted inputs in a security decision. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.0 is able to resolve this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

A memory-safety flaw in the key-management request-building component of the library can lead to an out-of-bounds write on the heap. A fixed-size output buffer is used under an assumption about cryptographic key size that is never validated, so when the library is embedded by a caller that supplies its own cryptographic callback implementation, data larger than the buffer can be written past its end. Exploitation requires the ability to control the embedding application's in-process key-management provider configuration, a high-privilege position. The demonstrated impact is memory corruption resulting in abnormal termination of the client process.

A flaw in the automatic client-side encryption schema generation of the Mongoid ODM may cause values that an application declared for encryption to be written and stored as cleartext when more than one model is mapped onto the same storage location. No error or warning is raised. A party holding an ordinary read-only database account, with no access to the encryption key material, may then obtain those values in clear form.

A Ruby object-document mapper does not apply its automatic field-level encryption configuration to certain fields when the data model uses class inheritance. Values the application designated for encryption are written to the database in readable form without any error or warning. A database account holding only read access to the application's collections, and no access to the encryption key store, may obtain those values.

A local user with an ordinary account on the same host can place a file in a shared temporary location that the JDBC driver's native library loading routine will accept and load without verifying its origin. Loading the driver class in a Java application may then run code of that user's choosing inside the application process, which may result in disclosure or alteration of data held by that process or in the process becoming unavailable.

A flaw was found in cpio. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering a stack-based buffer overflow when creating archives in tar or ustar formats. When archiving files owned by users or groups with names exceeding 32 characters, cpio copies these names into fixed-size memory without verifying their length. This unbounded copy corrupts stack memory and causes the application to crash.

The MongoDB Node.js driver does not consistently enforce its permitted-host restriction during OIDC authentication. A bearer token produced by the embedding application's own login callback may therefore be transmitted to a host outside the configured set of permitted hosts, which may result in unintended disclosure of that credential. No database account is required; the party supplying the connection configuration needs only to influence the settings the application passes to the driver.

A validation flaw in the DNS SRV host discovery of the MongoDB Node.js driver may cause the driver to connect to a host outside the expected domain. For a mongodb+srv:// connection string, the driver checks each host name in the DNS SRV response against the domain of the connection string. The driver then builds the connection address from the original name, in which certain characters end the host name early. An unauthenticated party who can forge or change the DNS SRV response may redirect the connection to a host of their choice. TLS does not prevent this, because the driver verifies the server certificate against the redirected host name. This may result in unintended disclosure of application data and authentication credentials, and in altered query results. Applications that use mongodb:// connection strings are not affected.

A MongoDB Rust Driver component that holds client-side field level encryption settings includes key management service credential material in its diagnostic formatting output without redaction. An application that records or displays this formatted output may place that material where a party with read access to the application's diagnostic output can see it, which may result in unintended disclosure of key material.

A deserialization type-restriction control in the BSON serialization component can be bypassed because the check used to recognize a class of compiler-generated types relies on an overly permissive heuristic rather than a precise identification. An unauthorized party able to supply BSON content that an application later deserializes into a loosely typed member can cause types outside the intended allow-list to be constructed and populated with unauthorized party-supplied values inside the consuming application. This can lead to unexpected object state and errors in downstream application logic. No elevated privileges beyond the ability to place unauthorized party-influenced content in the deserialization path are required.

Zipline before 4.8.0 contains a race condition vulnerability in src/server/routes/raw/[id].ts that allows remote attackers to bypass file maxViews limits through non-atomic view counting. Attackers holding a file link can send parallel requests that read the same pre-increment count, viewing view-limited or delete-on-max-views files beyond their limit.

Zipline before 4.6.5 contains a TOCTOU race condition in the POST /api/setup endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to create multiple SUPERADMIN accounts by racing concurrent requests before the firstSetup flag is reset. Attackers can send simultaneous requests with spoofed X-Forwarded-For headers during the argon2 hashing window to gain full administrative control of the instance.

Zipline before 4.6.4 contains a resource allocation vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass chunked-upload size and quota checks by forging Content-Range offsets and totals. Attackers can send tiny chunks to the partial upload endpoint with large declared offsets, causing the server to create oversized files and exhaust disk space.

Zipline through 4.6.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to read superadmin secrets because GET /api/users and GET /api/users/:id lack the canInteract check. Attackers can retrieve plaintext totpSecret and OAuth tokens to bypass 2FA and take over superadmin accounts, while any authenticated user can enumerate other users' folders via GET /api/user/folders.

Zipline before 4.6.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in POST /api/user/folders that allows authenticated users to reparent other users' files by supplying their file IDs. Attackers can harvest file IDs from public folders and create a folder seeded with them, disclosing victims' file URLs and removing those files from their folder views.

Zipline before 4.5.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the HighlightCode component that renders unescaped file content before highlight.js finishes loading. Authenticated attackers can upload text files containing HTML/JavaScript payloads that execute in viewers' browsers, enabling API calls such as account changes on the victim's behalf.

Zipline from 4.3.0 before 4.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to inject HTML through unescaped embed settings in SSR meta tags. Attackers can set malicious embedTitle, embedDescription, embedSiteName, or embedColor values via PATCH /api/user to execute JavaScript in browsers of visitors opening their file view pages.

Zipline before 4.5.0 contains a stored open redirect vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set arbitrary short URL destinations by abusing missing scheme validation in POST /api/user/urls. Attackers can store javascript: URIs or attacker-controlled URLs as destinations, causing visitors of the trusted short link to be redirected to phishing or malware pages.

Zipline before 4.5.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability caused by missing ownership verification in the PATCH and DELETE handlers for /api/user/folders/:id. Authenticated attackers can supply another user's folder ID to rename it, make it public, enable uploads, or delete it.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allows authenticated users to overwrite existing uploads by supplying unsanitized names. Attackers can submit names like ../uploads/victim.txt that bypass the raw-string database uniqueness check but normalize via path.join(), causing fs.rename() to replace other files' contents.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to delete arbitrary server files by injecting traversal sequences via the x-zipline-file-extension header. Attackers can upload a file with a poisoned stored name and short expiry so LocalDatasource deletion removes chosen files, causing denial of service or data loss.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read arbitrary server files by abusing a fallback treating the :id parameter as a datasource key. Attackers can send encoded traversal sequences in the :id of GET /api/user/files/:id/raw to escape the Local datasource uploads directory and read files like /etc/shadow.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the WebAuthn login endpoint that creates sessions for a supplied registered credential ID without verifying the assertion. Attackers who obtain a target's passkey credential ID can impersonate that account without its authenticator, potentially gaining administrative control over SUPERADMIN accounts.

Glance from 0.7.9 before 0.8.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious extension endpoints to inject javascript: URLs via the Widget-Title-URL response header. Attackers controlling an extension endpoint can execute script when users click the widget title, reading dashboard pages through same-origin requests and exfiltrating content.

Glance from 0.8.0 before 0.8.8 contains an observable response discrepancy in handlePageRequest and handlePageContentRequest that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate configured page slugs. Attackers can request candidate names against /{page} or /api/pages/{page}/content/ and compare 303/401 versus 404 status codes to discover hidden page names.

A type allow-list bypass in the BSON serialization library of the MongoDB C# Driver allows a type-restriction check to be circumvented when polymorphic data is deserialized into loosely typed members. An unauthorized party who can supply or plant BSON/JSON data that the application later deserializes can cause the application process to instantiate .NET types outside the intended allow-list and populate them with unauthorized party-controlled values. In applications that contain a suitable gadget type, this can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the application, with corresponding loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability. No special privileges beyond the ability to introduce data the application reads are required.

The Wikidata Lookup expansion module (wiki.py) in MISP misp-modules contained a SPARQL injection vulnerability. The handler function constructed a SPARQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied text value into the query string without any escaping or parameterization: 'SELECT ?item WHERE { ?item rdfs:label"' + request.get("text") + '" @en }'. An authenticated MISP user with access to the module could supply a crafted text attribute value containing SPARQL syntax (quotes, closing braces, UNION, SERVICE, LIMIT, etc.) to alter the structure of the query sent to the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint. This could allow an attacker to modify the query logic, extract unintended data, or cause the query to fail in ways that expose internal error details. Additionally, the old error handling path formatted raw exception objects into the response string ('wikidata API not accessible {}'.format(e)), potentially leaking internal information such as proxy credentials, query contents, or response bodies. The module also used a spoofed browser user-agent string and the deprecated Wikidata endpoint. The vulnerability required authenticated access to the MISP instance and the ability to invoke the wiki expansion module with a text attribute. The impact is limited to manipulation of the enrichment query and potential disclosure of internal error details; it does not directly compromise the MISP server or its stored data.

A security flaw has been discovered in SiteServer SSCMS up to 7.2.2. Impacted is an unknown function of the file /api/v1/captcha. Performing a manipulation of the argument Value results in inadequate encryption strength. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in JeecgBoot up to 3.9.6. This affects the function RestTemplate.exchange of the file org/jeecg/modules/airag/flow/c/a.class of the component flow-run Endpoint. The manipulation leads to server-side request forgery. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

The MISP Modules website component exposes external tool management endpoints (add, delete, change status, and change configuration) that did not enforce the optional administrator authentication policy. When ADMIN_PASSWORD was configured in the application environment, the module configuration endpoints correctly required an authenticated administrator session, but the external tools management handlers processed requests from anonymous users without any authorization check. An unauthenticated attacker with network access to the website could add arbitrary external tools, delete existing tools, toggle their active status, and modify their configurations including API keys and ingestion URLs. This inconsistency allowed bypass of the intended access control for the external tools management functionality. The vulnerability is conditional on ADMIN_PASSWORD being set; installations without an admin password intentionally permit open management access by design. The affected component is the external_tools Flask blueprint within the MISP Modules website application.

A flaw was found in freeradius's Extensible Authentication Protocol Method for Subscriber Identity Module (EAP-SIM) module. When handling authentication requests, the server copies a client-supplied identity into an internal structure without properly checking its length against a fixed-size buffer. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by sending specially crafted EAP-SIM messages, triggering a stack buffer overflow that crashes the service and results in a Denial of Service (DoS).

In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.

Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the myGESTIÓN Time Tracking module. The server skips the permission check when processing the “worker” parameter. By modifying this parameter, an authenticated user can view other users' time logs, including those of administrators.

Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the STEL Order Tempo module. The server retrieves data based on the `empleadoId` parameter without checking the user's permissions. By modifying this parameter, an authenticated user can view the first name, last name, role, job title, and vacation days of other employees.

The MISP Modules website component contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the external tools management interface. The /external_tools/list endpoint returned stored API keys (the api_key field) in its JSON response via the ExternalTools model serializer. Additionally, the browser-based edit form pre-populated the API key input field with the stored credential value, exposing it in the DOM.
