In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the authentication decorators for feed-key requests (auth_feedkey_func in website/decorators.py) and API-key requests (auth_func in website/web/api/v1/common.py) called Flask-Login's login_user() function. This caused the HTTP response to a request authenticated solely by a feed key (supplied as the X-FEED-KEY URL parameter) or an API key (supplied as the X-API-KEY header) to set a session cookie that grants full authenticated access to every page in the application, without requiring a password or two-factor authentication.

The practical impact is that any party possessing a leaked feed URL (a common occurrence, as feed URLs are shared with RSS readers) or an API key could obtain a valid web session for the associated account. This session provides access to the user's account page, which exposes the API key and other profile data, and for accounts with the administrator role, access to the /admin interface, enabling full administrative control of the application.

The vulnerability affects all users whose feed key or API key is exposed. No prior authentication, user interaction, or special network conditions are required; a single HTTP request with the token is sufficient to establish the session. The session persists until it expires, and because it is not bound to the original credential (a related CWE-613 issue noted by the developers), revoking the feed key or API key does not invalidate the already-created session.

The fix replaces the login_user() call with assignment to g._login_user, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads for the current request only, without writing any session cookie. The affected views remain unchanged and continue to see the authenticated user for the single request.

In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the Flask-Login session identifier was set to the bare numeric user ID (User.get_id() returned self.id). Because the session ID contained no component derived from the user's credential, it remained valid indefinitely regardless of any subsequent password change, account recovery, or administrator-initiated password reset. An attacker who had obtained a valid session for a user account (for example through cross-site scripting, session hijacking, or a previously exposed feed or API key) could continue to access that user's account after the user changed their password, because the session cookie still carried the same static user ID and the user_loader accepted it without any credential-bound validation.

The affected component is the session management layer of the vulnerability-lookup Flask application, specifically the User.get_id() method in website/models/user.py and the load_user callback in website/web/views/session_mgmt.py. The vulnerability required that an attacker already possessed a valid session for the target user; no additional authentication or special deployment configuration was needed beyond a standard deployment of the application.

The security impact is that a user cannot effectively revoke an attacker's access by changing their password, performing an account recovery, or having an administrator reset the credential. The attacker retains full authenticated access to the user's profile, subscriptions, and any role-gated functionality for the lifetime of the session cookie. Additionally, sessions that were opened via a feed key or API key before a prior fix (commit 3605d5b6) also persisted indefinitely.

The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

SeaweedFS before 4.42 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the VolumeServer.FetchAndWriteNeedle gRPC method that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the incomplete CVE-2026-73080 fix. Attackers can supply crafted replicas[].url entries or an azure_endpoint to make the volume server send requests with controlled tokens and bodies to internal services and metadata addresses.

SeaweedFS before 4.42 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to probe local files by supplying a filesystem path in gcs_google_application_credentials. Attackers can send crafted gRPC FetchAndWriteNeedle requests and use differing error messages to learn file existence, readability, and partial content shape on the host.

LimeSurvey before 6.17.16+260814 and 7.x before 7.0.10+260813 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the public statistics page via POST parameter names. Attackers can submit backtick-containing parameter names to buildSelects() and use blind techniques to read administrator password hashes and survey responses on MySQL or MariaDB.

RedAmon 4.0.0 before 7.8.0 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to control other tenants' agent sessions by supplying arbitrary session ids. Attackers can call /api/agent/sessions, interact and kill routes to list, kill, or send commands into other users' meterpreter and shell sessions on their compromised targets.

RedAmon before 7.8.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the kali-sandbox terminal server that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain a root shell by connecting to its WebSocket listener on port 8016. Attackers who can reach the port from co-resident containers or the host loopback can send keystrokes to an interactive /bin/bash session, executing commands as root inside the kali-sandbox container.

wallabag 2.3.3 before 2.6.16 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through article author metadata rendered with Twig raw in entry.html.twig. Attackers can embed HTML event handlers in a web page's author metadata so scripts run in a victim's wallabag session when the saved entry is opened, exposing their data.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a heap buffer overflow in ReadBinaryData() in jxrgluelib/JXRMeta.c caused by integer overflow of the metadata count. Attackers can supply a JPEG XR file with a count of 0xFFFFFFFE or 0xFFFFFFFF, wrapping PKAlloc(uCount + 2) to an undersized buffer that the following file read overflows, corrupting heap memory in decoding applications.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.6 contain a stack buffer over-read vulnerability in ReadWMIHeader() in image/decode/strdec.c due to an unterminated signature buffer. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file whose 8 signature bytes contain no zero byte, causing strstr to read past the stack buffer and potentially crash the application.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in ImageStrDecDecode() in image/decode/strdec.c. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file declaring a colour format with no channels, leaving p1MBbuffer[0] NULL and crashing the decoder via memset.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.7 contain a reachable assertion vulnerability in ParsePFDEntry() that allows attackers to abort applications via an invalid orientation tag. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range WMP_tagTransformation value to crash applications using default assertion-enabled builds, or store an unchecked orientation value otherwise.

'@tinacms/graphql 2.2.2 through 4.1.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the content root by following pre-existing dangling symlinks. Attackers can create documents through the GraphQL API targeting a dangling symlink, bypassing assertWithinBase checks, to write controlled content such as authorized_keys to server-writable locations.

Koillection before 1.8.6 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view objects nested under private parents through the shared search autocomplete route. Attackers can query GET /user/{username}/search/autocomplete/{term}, whose native SQL filters on visibility instead of final_visibility, to obtain names, ids and counts of hidden collections, items, albums and wishlists.

GitBucket through 4.48.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to edit and merge other users' pull requests because the PATCH pulls and PUT pulls merge REST API endpoints only check read access. Attackers can close, reopen, retitle, retarget, or merge pull requests into the base branch without write permission on public repositories or as private-repository guest collaborators.

Frappe CRM before 1.84.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_deal_contacts method that allows authenticated low-privileged users to read contacts of deals they cannot access. Attackers can supply or iterate CRM Deal names to obtain linked contacts' full names, email addresses, and mobile numbers, bypassing row-level permission rules.

Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in DataSourceController.testConnect that allows any authenticated user to open arbitrary JDBC connections by supplying caller-controlled connection settings. Attackers can probe internal hosts and ports via returned driver errors, or supply a MySQL JDBC URL enabling local-infile against a malicious server to read files from the Dinky host.

Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ClusterConfigurationController that allows authenticated users without cluster configuration permissions to list Flink cluster configurations. Attackers can query the /api/clusterConfiguration/list and listAll endpoints to retrieve full configJson deployment settings for every cluster in their tenant.

Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject script by abusing #topic link wrapping in preparePost and parsePostTag. Attackers can publish posts or comments with a crafted topic containing a lone '<' and event handler to steal the PAOPAO_TOKEN JWT from localStorage and take over viewer accounts.

Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 fails to validate the attachment_price field when creating posts, allowing authenticated users to set negative prices on charge attachments. Attackers with two ordinary accounts can download the attachment via GET /v1/attachment, where the negative price increases the buyer's wallet balance, minting funds to purchase other users' paid attachments.

SamWaf 1.0.128 through 1.3.25-beta.11 contains a request body inspection bypass vulnerability in WafEngine.ServeHTTP that skips bodies with chunked encoding or lengths of 2048 bytes or more. Remote unauthenticated attackers can send SQL injection, XSS, command injection, traversal or upload payloads chunked or padded, which reach the protected backend uninspected.

Rocboss paopao-ce 0.2.0 through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a path traversal vulnerability in LocalOSS DeleteObject that allows authenticated users to delete arbitrary files by submitting crafted media values. Attackers can send dot-dot-slash sequences in the avatar or media content to POST /v1/user/avatar or POST /v1/post/comment, deleting server-writable files including configuration and data.

Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain paid attachments by reading storage URLs from the GET /v1/post endpoint. Attackers can download the paid file directly from the unauthenticated LocalOSS /oss static route, whose signed URL expired parameter is never checked.

REBUILD 2.7.0 through 4.5.4 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject AjQL conditions through the plan parameter of /project/tasks/list. Attackers can use priority-* plans and the returned task count as a boolean oracle to recover a task creator's SHA-256 password hash and log in as that user, including the administrator.

REBUILD 4.3.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to obtain a SYSTEM_USER token by requesting /commons/file-preview with an arbitrary src value. Attackers can read the leaked _csrfToken from the redirect Location header and send it as X-AuthToken to access the admin center and administrative APIs.

REBUILD 3.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify their own roleId through mass assignment in /app/entity/record-save and /app/entity/common-save. Attackers can submit their own User record with roleId set to the built-in administrator role, bypassing updatable=false restrictions to gain full administrator privileges.

REBUILD 4.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to recover the administrator password hash by filtering User.password through the MCP QueryRecords tool. Attackers can send LK2 prefix-match filters to the /gw/mcp/sse gateway and use the returned total count as an oracle to extract the SHA-256 hash one character at a time, then log in as administrator.

OfficeCLI 1.0.56 through 1.0.161 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the officecli watch preview that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped numbering w:color values. Attackers can craft a DOCX whose color closes the style element, then abuse the unauthenticated /api/batch endpoint to read local files and modify the watched document.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve server secrets through the /api/v1/config/defaults endpoint. Attackers can send a GET request to obtain the operator's LLM provider API keys and GitHub or GitLab tokens, then abuse those services and accessible repositories.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in ReportGenerator.generate_task_report that allows registered users to read server files and perform SSRF. Attackers can create a project whose name contains a link attachment element and download the task PDF report to retrieve local files or internal network responses.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write arbitrary files by importing projects with crafted IDs. Attackers can set absolute or ../ project IDs via /api/v1/database/import, then upload ZIPs through /api/v1/scan/upload-zip following cloned symlinks to overwrite app/main.py for remote code execution.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in ChangeManager.last_changes() that exposes workspaces the viewer cannot view by skipping Workspace.can_view() checks site-wide. Anonymous visitors on instances with REQUIRE_LOGIN disabled and only public projects can query /changes/, /api/changes/, or RSS/CSV feeds to obtain hidden workspace names, UUIDs, actions, and timestamps.

Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 contains a hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge signed data by using the publicly known Django SECRET_KEY in tcms/settings/common.py. Attackers can forge or tamper with signed cookie-based messages and django.core.signing payloads, weakening password-reset and session-authentication HMACs on deployments keeping the default.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to send users to arbitrary sites by supplying an unvalidated redirectUri parameter on the /pay/[id] payment link page. Attackers can distribute payment links with a malicious redirectUri that PayPageWidget opens via window.open after payment without noopener, enabling phishing and reverse tabnabbing of the payment page.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

Unrolled Secure before 1.18.0 contains an SSLRedirect bypass vulnerability in Secure.isSSL() that trusts the client-supplied r.URL.Scheme to determine HTTPS transport. Attackers can send plaintext HTTP requests with an absolute-form https:// request-target to skip the HTTPS redirect and have application responses served unencrypted.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in revalidatePathAction and revalidateCacheTagAction server actions in revalidate.ts. Unauthenticated attackers can use action identifiers exposed in the client bundle to send POST requests that purge cached pages and data, forcing repeated regeneration and degrading performance.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read non-public team metadata by requesting the team join page with any invite ID. Attackers who know a team slug can obtain the serialized Team object, exposing billing email, billing status, Stripe customer ID, verified domain and support identifiers.

Cetmix Tower through 17.0.3.0.0 and 18.0 before 18.0.4.0.1 contains an improper SSH host key verification vulnerability in SSHConnection.connect() that falls back to Paramiko's AutoAddPolicy when no host key is pinned. On-path attackers using ARP or DNS spoofing can present their own host key during Skip Host Key or Get from Host connections to capture stored SSH passwords and tamper with commands and files.

Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in its mount namespace (mnt ns) caching logic. When resolving a security event that references a specific process PID and an expected mount namespace, the Switcher::new function read /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt to determine the target namespace and cached the result under the expected namespace key without verifying that the resolved namespace actually matched the expected one.

An attacker with local access could exploit this by either (1) arranging for the referenced PID to be reused by a process in a different namespace (e.g., the host namespace) before Kunai resolves it, or (2) calling unshare or setns on the target process after the event is generated but before the namespace is resolved. In either case, the wrong namespace (potentially the host's own namespace) would be cached under the container's namespace key.

The security impact is that subsequent container security events would be resolved against host filesystem paths rather than container paths. This undermines the integrity of the security monitoring data: container activity could be misattributed to the host, host activity could be misattributed to a container, and file-path-based detections or alerts would reference incorrect paths. An attacker could potentially use this to obscure malicious activity within a container by making it appear as benign host activity, or to generate misleading security alerts.

The vulnerability requires local access to the system and a specific timing window between event generation and namespace resolution. No remote attack vector or user interaction is required.

Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the unauthenticated GET /prime/redirect route that allows remote attackers to redirect users to external sites. Attackers can craft links with a 36-character id and arbitrary url parameter on the trusted Prime host to send victims to phishing sites.

Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register accounts via the createUser mutation on /prime/graphql. Because the isAuthenticated() guard has its check commented out and createAbility() hard-codes every role to admin, attackers can log in with full administrative control over content, users, webhooks and settings.

Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to invoke privileged GraphQL mutations because the @Authorized() decorator is omitted. Attackers can call updateWebhook, createRelease, unpublishDocument and updateUser at /prime/graphql to create releases and, with a record UUID, redirect webhooks, unpublish documents, or overwrite user profiles.

Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the updateSystem GraphQL mutation that allows authenticated administrators to execute shell commands via the package version string. Attackers can append shell metacharacters to the unvalidated version value, which is passed to child_process.exec() in yarn add or npm install commands, executing commands as the server process.

Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the getIsPathValid function that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access sibling paths sharing a content directory name prefix. Attackers can send requests with a no-cors header to the blob, update, and tree handlers under /api/keystatic to read, create, overwrite, or delete files such as posts-evil/pwn.yaml.

Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the githubOauthCallback handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to sign victims in with the attacker's GitHub account by omitting state validation. Attackers can induce victims to visit the OAuth callback with an attacker-obtained authorization code, causing victim edits in the admin UI to be committed under the attacker's GitHub identity.

Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the DocumentRenderer component that allows authenticated content editors to inject scripts via unvalidated link href values. Editors can paste anchors with javascript: URLs into document fields, executing script when visitors click rendered links and stealing the keystatic-gh-access-token cookie.

Contentlayer @contentlayer/core through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JavaScript by embedding single quotes in content file names. Attackers can add a content file whose name breaks out of the import specifier in makeDataExportFile(), executing injected code when contentlayer dev or a Next.js dev server imports the generated module.

Contentlayer @contentlayer/source-files through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers who control content files to execute JavaScript by abusing gray-matter's still-enabled JavaScript engine in parseMarkdown(). Attackers can start a Markdown or MDX file with a ---js or ---javascript frontmatter delimiter to run code during build, exposing CI build secrets.

Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject unsanitized HTML into Markdown cells. Attackers can store iframe, object, or form elements with javascript: URLs that execute when administrators view the table, stealing Firebase sessions.

Rowy through 3.0.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability in default Firebase Storage rules that grants any user holding a role read and write access to the entire bucket. Authenticated users restricted to a single table or read-only access can use the Firebase SDK directly to list, download, overwrite, and delete any stored files.

Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject scripts via URL field links lacking scheme validation. Attackers can store values like javascript: URIs containing the string http in URL cells, executing script when victims click the open-link button to steal Firebase sessions.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain administrator access by forging JWTs with the hardcoded 'nodepress-secret' fallback key. Attackers can sign HS256 bearer tokens with the default issuer, audience, and role 'admin' to access administrator-only APIs for article, comment, options, and file management.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade throttling by spoofing the X-Forwarded-For header, because trustProxy is enabled. Attackers can send X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 or rotate values to brute-force the administrator password via POST /admin/login and evade comment IP blocklists.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in linesToEmailContent() that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject markup into notification emails because comment content is not escaped. Attackers can post comments or replies via POST /comments containing forged links, images, or tracking resources rendered in administrator and author mail clients from the blog's address.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator access by using the hardcoded default password 'root'. Attackers can send base64-encoded 'root' to POST /admin/login when NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD is unset to obtain admin tokens and fully control the site.

Sandboxie-Plus before 1.18.6 contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability in SbieSvc that allows standard users to launch UpdUtil.exe as SYSTEM via MSGID_PROCESS_RUN_UPDATER requests. Attackers can inject code into a signed SandMan.exe process to bypass the signature check and write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary paths, achieving SYSTEM code execution.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.0.0 before 9.2.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in back-office theme and module archive import that allows authenticated employees to write files outside intended directories. Attackers can craft a theme name in config/theme.yml or upload a module archive extracted before validation to place PHP files in web-accessible locations and execute code.
Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

The CourseCure Courses plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 1.5.1. This is due to a missing capability check in the ajax_save_settings() function, which accepts arbitrary POST parameters and calls update_option() with attacker-controlled keys and values without any authorization verification. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to elevate their privileges to administrator by setting the default_role WordPress option to 'administrator' and users_can_register to '1', then registering a new account that is automatically granted full administrator access.

An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

Ivanti Endpoint Manager (EPM) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability that could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to leak specific stored credential data.

MCUboot's serial-recovery image-upload handler bs_upload() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c declares const struct flash_area *fap = NULL and assigns it only via flash_area_open() part-way through the function. Two early validation failures (goto out_invalid_data) — a CBOR map that fails to decode, or an upload packet missing the off/data members — branch past the open while fap is still NULL, then fall into the shared epilogue. In MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES builds that epilogue unconditionally calls boot_handle_enc_fw(fap), which reaches boot_image_load_header() and flash_area_read() and dereferences the NULL flash_area.

The defect is reachable pre-authentication: the trigger is the very first serial-recovery upload command carrying a malformed payload. The guarding conditions are default-true on a fresh recovery session — img_num, curr_off and img_size are zero-initialized statics, so curr_off == img_size and the primary-slot test both hold. It requires a non-default build: encrypted images (MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES / Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE) together with an active serial-recovery transport, on the Zephyr or Mynewt port (the two that build both boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c and boot_serial_encryption.c with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES).

The impact is a transient denial of service of the bootloader during recovery. fap is a hard NULL rather than an attacker-controlled value, so there is no memory-corruption or information-leak primitive and image authentication is unaffected. Whether the dereference faults is platform-dependent — on targets where address 0x0 is mapped readable flash the read merely returns an error and execution continues, while targets that trap NULL (MPU / null-pointer-exception detection) take a hard fault. Because serial recovery is unauthenticated by design and already permits the console attacker to write the secondary slot, the added capability is only a low-value transient crash.

The related unconditional flash_area_close(fap) call in the same epilogue is a safe no-op on the ports that reach it, so it does not contribute to the dereference.

The affected ports are the Zephyr port — boot/zephyr/CMakeLists.txt compiles boot_serial.c under CONFIG_MCUBOOT_SERIAL and boot_serial_encryption.c under CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE — and the Mynewt port, whose mcuboot_config.h defines MCUBOOT_SERIAL unconditionally and MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES under any BOOTUTIL_ENCRYPT_ syscfg, with boot/boot_serial/pkg.yml declaring no explicit source list so the whole directory is built. The Espressif port is not affected**: it compiles boot_serial.c but not boot_serial_encryption.c, and defines no MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES, so the #ifdef MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES block containing the call is preprocessed away. The NuttX, Cypress and Mbed ports do not build boot_serial.c at all.

boot_save_boot_status() in boot/bootutil/src/boot_record.c reads the image's EXPECTED_HASH_TLV into a stack buffer image_hash[IMAGE_HASH_SIZE] that is never zero-initialised. The TLV handler validates only the upper bound (len > sizeof(image_hash)) and then reads exactly len bytes, so a TLV shorter than IMAGE_HASH_SIZE leaves the tail of image_hash holding stale stack content. The subsequent copy into the boot record, memcpy(buf + offset, image_hash, sizeof(image_hash)), uses the fixed buffer size rather than len, so up to IMAGE_HASH_SIZE - 1 bytes of uninitialised bootloader stack are written into the measured-boot record.

The defect is reachable only under MCUBOOT_MEASURED_BOOT, and only when nothing has checked the length of the hash TLV before boot_save_boot_status() reads it. bootutil_img_validate() rejects a hash TLV whose length is not exactly sizeof(hash) (boot/bootutil/src/image_validate.c:345), and primary-slot validation is on by default (Zephyr's CONFIG_BOOT_VALIDATE_SLOT0 defaults to y), so in a default build the malformed image never reaches this code. Two kinds of build let a short TLV through:

Builds that use pure signatures (MCUBOOT_SIGN_PURE, Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_SIGNATURE_TYPE_PURE). The signature covers the image itself, so the hash-TLV check in bootutil_img_validate() is compiled out, and a pure-signed image normally carries no hash TLV. A hash TLV is still allowed in the unprotected TLV area, which the signature does not cover, so a short one can be added to a correctly signed image without invalidating it. This applies with every upgrade strategy, including direct-XIP and RAM-load, and the modified image can be delivered through any path that accepts a signed image.
Builds with primary-slot validation turned off: the swap and overwrite loader built without MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT, which checks only the image magic before calling boot_add_shared_data(), and the Zephyr single-slot loader (boot/zephyr/single_loader.c) built without it, including the MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT_ONCE variant, which skips validation once the trailer records an earlier successful one. Placing the crafted image requires physical or flash-write access to the device; in a single-slot build with serial recovery enabled, the serial-recovery upload writes the primary slot directly and can place it as well. Outside pure-signature builds, the direct-XIP and RAM-load strategies in boot/bootutil/src/loader.c validate the selected slot unconditionally and are not affected.

It is also reachable through a time-of-check/time-of-use change to tamperable external flash between validation and the boot-record read.

In these configurations the boot record's measurement is already not trustworthy: the hash copied into the record is the image's own EXPECTED_HASH_TLV, which nothing has verified and which the attacker chooses. The defect therefore does not weaken attestation integrity any further. What it adds is a path for bootloader memory to leave the device: up to 63 bytes (IMAGE_HASH_SIZE - 1) of uninitialised bootloader stack are embedded in the measurement field that a downstream attestation service sends to a remote verifier. In the configurations analysed the residue is bootloader internal state (TLV offsets and lengths, flash addresses, loop state), not key material, but what occupies that stack region depends on configuration and on which code ran before boot_save_boot_status(). It is reported as a low-severity, defense-in-depth disclosure with no integrity or availability impact.

This is distinct from the already-fixed record_len integer underflow in the same routine (GHSA-8hrv-4cp5-4rg3). The fix rejects any EXPECTED_HASH_TLV whose length is not exactly IMAGE_HASH_SIZE.

MCUboot's Zephyr serial-recovery upload handler bs_upload() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c decodes the host-supplied image field of an MCUmgr image-upload request into img_num (a full 32-bit value) and latches it on the off == 0 packet without any range check. It then passes img_num straight to flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0), which on the Zephyr port resolves to __flash_area_ids_for_slot() in boot/zephyr/include/sysflash/sysflash.h and indexes the static const int all_slots[] table as all_slots[img_num  2]. That table holds only MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER  2 entries, so any img_num >= MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER is an out-of-bounds read.

The path is reachable by anyone with access to the serial / SMP recovery console, which is unauthenticated by design, and the bad value is supplied before any image signature is verified. The defect is specific to the default non-direct upload path (MCUBOOT_SERIAL_DIRECT_IMAGE_UPLOAD disabled) on the Zephyr port with the array-backed slot layout (not CONFIG_SINGLE_APPLICATION_SLOT). It is not gated on a multi-image configuration: MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER defaults to 1, so even a default single-image build is affected for any image >= 1. The MCUBOOT_SERIAL_DIRECT_IMAGE_UPLOAD path is safe (its flash_area_id_from_direct_image() switch returns -EINVAL for unknown indices).

flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot() takes a signed int image_index while img_num is uint32_t, so the attacker controls the sign of the index as well as its magnitude: an image of 0xFFFFFFFE converts to -2 and reads all_slots[-4], off the front of the table, while large positive values read off the end (CWE-192). (0xFFFFFFFF itself is the "no image given" sentinel and selects image 0.) Either way the index multiply img * 2 is performed in int, so a wild offset yields a bus/hard fault, giving a reliable denial of service of the bootloader during recovery. For moderately out-of-range indices the read returns adjacent .rodata as a garbage flash-area id that is handed to flash_area_open(); this normally fails with MGMT_ERR_EINVAL, but if the garbage id happens to match a valid non-image partition, the subsequent erase/write can target a partition outside the image set (CWE-787). The attacker-supplied value is never echoed back, so there is no information disclosure. The fix is to reject img_num >= BOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER on the off == 0 packet, before the slot lookup. The comparison must be made on the unsigned img_num: an equivalent guard applied after the conversion to int would not reject the negative case above. __flash_area_ids_for_slot() should bounds-check its own arguments as defence in depth.
This vulnerability was reported independently twice: by NVIDIA Project Vanessa on 2026-06-22, and by Kai Phan (@kaimandalic) on 2026-07-19 as GHSA-8v33-88p6-jffj, which is closed as a duplicate of this advisory. Both original reports are reproduced in full below.

split_image_check() in boot/bootutil/src/loader.c declares a fixed uint8_t loader_hash[32] buffer and passes it as the out_hash out-parameter to bootutil_img_validate(). That routine copies IMAGE_HASH_SIZE bytes into out_hash (memcpy(out_hash, hash, IMAGE_HASH_SIZE) in boot/bootutil/src/image_validate.c), where IMAGE_HASH_SIZE is a compile-time constant of 64 for MCUBOOT_SHA512 or 48 for MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384/SHA-384 (boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/sha.h). The buffer tracks SHA-256 (32 bytes) while the copy length tracks the configured algorithm, so the write overruns the buffer by 16 or 32 bytes.

The overflow is only present in a non-default configuration: the legacy Mynewt split-image feature must be compiled (split_go()/split_image_check(), i.e. neither MCUBOOT_DIRECT_XIP nor MCUBOOT_RAM_LOAD), the digest must be larger than 32 bytes (MCUBOOT_SHA512 or MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384), and MCUBOOT_SIGN_PURE must be off. split_go() is a public API with no caller inside MCUboot; it is invoked from a Mynewt application. In the default SHA-256 build there is no overflow.

The over-written bytes are the one-way digest of the loader image and the overflow length is fixed at build time, so the contents are not meaningfully attacker-controlled and the size is not attacker-chosen. The realistic impact is bounded, uncontrolled corruption of the bootloader's stack on the split-boot path, manifesting as instability or failed boot in the affected configuration rather than reliable code execution. The fix is to size loader_hash to IMAGE_HASH_SIZE and pass IMAGE_HASH_SIZE as the matching seed length.

BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS) and Privileged Remote Access (PRA)contain an OS command injection vulnerability. Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating system commands in the context of the site user. Successful exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction and may lead to system compromise, including unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and service disruption.

The MemberDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.7. This is due to a mass-assignment vulnerability in the `user_account_manager()` function's edit_profile branch, where all submitted `$_POST` fields are iterated and directly assigned to the current member object via the `MS_Model` `__set()` magic method with no field allowlist and no capability or ownership check on the submitted `id` parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject an arbitrary user ID via the `id` parameter — overwriting any WordPress user's email address and password, including the site administrator's — and subsequently use those modified credentials to gain full administrative access to the site.

A flaw was found in yggdrasil-worker-package-manager. An authenticated attacker can exploit this issue to achieve arbitrary file modification or potential privilege escalation. The vulnerability exists because repository management operations fail to sanitize directory traversal sequences (such as '../') within repository names. By supplying a crafted repository name, an attacker can manipulate the root-level worker process into creating or deleting files outside the intended directory, compromising host system integrity.

LibreOffice supports fonts embedded in documents. When a document is exported to PDF, the fonts it uses are embedded in the PDF, and a font in CFF (Compact Font Format) is converted to another font format on the way. An out-of-bounds write existed when the charstring program of a crafted font was interpreted, because some indexes and ranges taken from the font were not checked against the size of the data they refer to. In fixed versions these indexes and ranges are checked, and a font that fails the checks is not converted.

LibreOffice can export documents to PDF protected by a password. With the PDF 2.0 option the file is encrypted with 256-bit AES, using a file encryption key and salts that are meant to be random. The key and the salts were drawn from a pseudo-random number generator that is not suitable for cryptography, so the encryption key of an exported PDF could be recovered without knowing the password. In fixed versions the key and the salts are drawn from the random source of the operating system.

LibreOffice has an option, called stealth mode in earlier advisories, that stops documents from outside the trusted file locations from loading linked images and other content. The option is not on by default. With the option on, a linked background image in an HTML document was still fetched while the document was imported. In fixed versions a linked background image is checked against the option like other linked images, and is not fetched when the option blocks it.

LibreOffice can import EMF, EMF+ and WMF images, which may be embedded in documents. Several out-of-bounds reads existed in the readers for these formats, because sizes, counts and offsets taken from a crafted image were not checked against the data the image actually holds. In fixed versions these values are checked against the size of each record and the data that remains, and a record that fails the checks is not used.

The Flatsome theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'data-text-sec', 'data-title', and 'title' Attributes via Custom HTML Block in all versions up to, and including, 3.20.12 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives server-side sanitization because wp_kses_post permits data-* attributes globally via _wp_add_global_attributes, allowing attacker-controlled values in data-text-sec, data-title, and title attributes to persist in saved post content and be later interpreted as HTML by the ux-countdown, scroll-to, and lightbox-gallery JavaScript behaviors.

The HashiCorp cap JWT validation library before version 0.14.0 is vulnerable to a claims validation bypass that may cause downstream applications to make authorization decisions using claim values different from those validated. Exploitation requires attacker-controlled claims in a JWT signed by a key trusted by the application. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-19194) is fixed in cap 0.14.0.

The Shipo plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions 1.6 through 1.8.0. This is due to the `authenticate_rest_user()` function parsing the `LOGGED_IN_COOKIE` value and authenticating the named user without verifying the cookie's cryptographic signature. The function's intended `/wp-json/shipo/` route restriction can also be bypassed by placing that substring in the query string of an unrelated REST endpoint. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know an existing username to impersonate that user, including an administrator, and perform authorized actions through the REST API, including creating another administrator account.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, there is a stack-based out-of-bounds write / stack-buffer-overflow in bacnet-stack when the server processes a malicious Atomic-Read-File request in record access mode. The bug is triggered on the real server side. A crafted request can set an excessively large RecordCount, which is later used as the loop bound for writing record data into a stack-allocated BACNET_ATOMIC_READ_FILE_DATA data structure. However, the stack object only has space for one fileData element. When the loop reaches i = 1, the code computes &data->fileData[1], which is already out of bounds, and the resulting invalid pointer is passed down to memmove(), causing a stack-buffer-overflow. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, there is a client-side out-of-bounds read in the AtomicReadFile-ACK record-access handling path. The issue is caused by a mismatch between a remote returnedRecordCount value and the fixed local fileData[] array capacity in BACNET_ATOMIC_READ_FILE_DATA. The ACK decode path preserves the remote RecordCount, discards storage for excess records without truncating that count, and a downstream sink later iterates over the original RecordCount and indexes fileData[i] out of bounds. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

Oracle E-Business Suite contains an improper privilege management vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Payments. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Payments.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, a remote attacker can trigger an uncontrolled recursion and stack overflow in the default server application of bacnet-stack by abusing the Channel object. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a RemoveListElement request targeting Notification-Class.recipient-list can trigger a stack-based out-of-bounds write in the current master branch when the request contains more than NC_MAX_RECIPIENTS valid BACnetDestination elements. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a stack-buffer-overflow can be triggered in the current master branch when a Loop object reads a referenced property through its default timer path and the referenced property is OBJECT_STRUCTURED_VIEW / PROP_DESCRIPTION containing a long attacker-controlled string. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor contains an improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, there is a remotely reachable denial-of-service vulnerability in bacnet-stack affecting the default demo server built from the unmodified apps/server/main.c. This issue has been patched in version 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.2 to before 1.4.5, and 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, a signed fileStartPosition taken from AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile stream-access requests is not validated tightly enough before it reaches the RAM file backends. Practical impact includes: reliable denial of service via process crash, out-of-bounds read that may expose adjacent memory contents, or out-of-bounds write that may corrupt heap memory and destabilize the process. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5 and 1.5.1.
Microsoft SharePoint contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability which could allow an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2, a reachable out-of-bounds write exists when encoding the device.address-binding property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, the bsc_node_parse_urls() function in src/bacnet/datalink/bsc/bsc-node.c contains three distinct bugs when parsing space-separated WebSocket URIs from a BACnet/SC Address Resolution ACK message. Two bugs cause out-of-bounds writes past the utf8_urls[10][129] array in the static BSC_ADDRESS_RESOLUTION structure. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the BACnet stack's ReadPropertyMultiple (RPM) handler. When processing a malformed RPM request packet that lacks the expected closing tags, the function handler_read_property_multiple enters an infinite loop. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, there is a library-level memory safety issue that is reachable from an unmodified official sample server (apps/server-basic/main.c) over BACnet/IP resulting in a stack-use-after-return in writable Device string properties. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
LiteSpeed cPanel plugin contains a UNIX symbolic link (Symlink) following vulnerability that could allow a user with FTP or web shell access on a shared hosting server running CloudLinux/CageFS.
Microsoft SharePoint contains a weak authentication vulnerability which allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

IBM Bob 2.0.3 allows unauthorized extensions to retrieve session tokens via the authentication provider API. The token is exposed in the account identifier field during account enumeration, without requiring explicit user consent. This may allow malicious extensions to access sensitive session information and potentially perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.
Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services contains an insufficient granularity of access control vulnerability that allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.
Microsoft SharePoint contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a BACnet/SC peer can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read (up to 3 bytes), pre-authentication, in the BACnet/SC header-option decoder. bvlc_sc_decode_proprietary_option() reads the vendor-id and option-type at fixed offsets [3],[4],[5] before checking the option's declared header length, and the option-list validator never enforces a minimum length for proprietary options. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, there is a remote global-buffer-overflow in the official router-ipv6 application shipped with bacnet-stack, this results in an out-of-bounds write to the global transmit buffer under ASan. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
Microsoft SharePoint contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to improper cryptographic signature verification in the JWT refresh logic. An authenticated low-privilege user can submit self-crafted​ ​JWT​ containing​ ​an existing user​ ​identifier and, due to the lack of signature validation,​​  obtain​ ​a ​​valid,​​ fully-signed​​ session ​​token​​ for​​ any ​​account ​​in​ ​the​ ​system. This allows the attacker to impersonate any user, including administrators.
This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Dynamic LINQ injection. Due to improper input validation, an authenticated attacker can inject conditional expressions into the sort parameter of paginated administrative endpoints. Analyzing the returned result order allows the attacker to extract value of any field character by character, leading to potential exposure of sensitive data.


This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Due to improper input validation, an authenticated attacker can inject malicious scripts into givenName and surname parameters via the /api/auth/profile endpoint. When an administrator visits the admin changelog logs, the injected script is automatically executed, in his browser.


This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored XSS via content parameter in Tiny editor functionality. Authenticated attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JS into website, which will be rendered/executed when user tries to edit changed entry.

This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored XSS in avatar upload functionality. Authenticated attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JS into website, which will be rendered/executed when visiting an URL leading to a edited avatar.

This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS restricts the ability to upload files via the UI to specific file types. However, an avatar upload functionality allows an attacker to upload files of any type and extension without restriction.
This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS sends JWT token via GET requests. This allows a local attacker with access to browser history to obtain valid JWT token and perform action on behalf of the victim. The token is valid for only short period of time; after that time, it expires and can no longer be used.



The vendor assessed the likelihood of exploitation as very low and determined that a fix is not necessary.

Edito CMS deserializes JSON data without further validation. A user (even an administrator) cannot exploit this vulnerability through the application's normal functionality. An attacker who could modify cache entries or inject them could execute code on the server.




This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.
Broadcom VMware vCenter contains a path traversal vulnerability which could allow a threat actor with network access to vCenter to execute arbitrary code.

Gitea contains a code injection vulnerability that allows an attacker with repository write access to send a malicious patch to the diffpatch API endpoint to plant an executable Git hook and run shell commands as the Gitea service account.

Dell SmartFabric OS10 Software, versions prior to 10.6.0.10, contains an Improper Access Control vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

Dell SmartFabric OS10 Software, versions prior to 10.6.0.10, contains an Incorrect Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command execution.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, lighting_command_decode in src/bacnet/lighting.c decodes its first field with the bounded apdu_size - apdu_len, but every nested decode in the operation switch is called with the original full apdu_size while the read pointer has been advanced to &apdu[apdu_len]. The leaf decoders bound their reads against the size they are told, so they read up to apdu_len bytes past the end of the caller's buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a remote out-of-bounds read exists in the official BACnet client application apps/readpropm in bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6. When readpropm sends a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request to a malicious BACnet/IP peer, the peer can reply with a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK that drives the client into a global-buffer-overflow read on the global receive buffer Rx_Buf. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a malformed but non-empty BACnet WriteProperty request can drive the official server demo into a non-terminating request-processing loop with repeated heap-backed side effects. This results in a remote unauthenticated denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption and a non-terminating request path. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE implementation accepts AtomicWriteFile(record-access) requests that replace existing records with caller-controlled content. If a client replaces a record with shorter data, the backend can shrink the heap allocation and then continue processing with a trailing-copy length derived from the old layout. During that replace path, the RAMFS backend computes the trailing-copy length from the old file layout, then shrinks the heap allocation, and finally uses the stale length in memmove(). As a result, the source range of that memmove() can extend beyond the end of the reallocated heap buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE object implementation stores appended records as NUL-terminated strings, but its record-counting logic later walks the buffer as if an additional terminating empty record were present. As a result, two consecutive AtomicWriteFile(record-access) append requests can cause record_count() to call bacnet_strnlen() on a pointer that is already one byte past the end of the heap allocation. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the BACnet FILE object implementation allows remote WriteProperty(PROP_FILE_SIZE) requests to change the size of a stream-access FILE object without checking whether that FILE is marked Read_Only. When the FILE backend is RAMFS, enlarging the file only performs realloc() and updates the stored size; the newly exposed tail region is not initialized before later reads. As a result, a remote client can enlarge a read-only RAMFS-backed stream-access FILE and then immediately retrieve the newly exposed region with AtomicReadFile(stream-access). Depending on the allocator and build configuration, the returned data may contain sanitizer fill bytes, stale heap contents, or other unintended process memory. Shrinking the file through the same path can also remotely truncate content that was intended to be read-only. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

RBH Access Technologies Integra32 Security Management System 5.1.11 R5.0 contains an unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability in its deprecated .NET Remoting service, exposed on TCP port 2001 via the AxcvcLt.dll library using BinaryServerFormatterSinkProvider at TypeFilterLevel.Full without requiring authentication. A remote unauthenticated attacker can send a malicious serialized gadget payload (such as a ysoserial.net TypeConfuseDelegate chain) to the IntegraURI object endpoint, or exploit MarshalByRefObject/MarshalByValue unmarshalling for arbitrary file read/write and SMB/NTLMv2 credential coercion, to achieve remote code execution as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and fully compromise the host.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge privileged actions such as administrator user creation by merging $_GET and $_POST parameters without requiring an anti-CSRF token. Attackers can craft a malicious link or auto-navigating page that issues a plain GET request, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection and SameSite=Lax cookie behavior on top-level navigations to create unauthorized administrator accounts.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private calendar data by exploiting a missing dateCrea value that causes the md5Id token to collapse to md5(calendarId.userId), both small enumerable integers. Attackers can compute valid tokens and request the misc&action=DisplayIcal endpoint with a forged md5Id to read any user's private calendar events without authentication.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs by manipulating the objUrl parameter in Ctrl.php's redir() function. Attackers can craft login links with objUrl set to a malicious site, causing the application to issue an HTTP 302 redirect to that external URL, which can be abused for phishing and credential theft.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious HTML markup by controlling imported directory data or an uploaded CSV file, as values are rendered into table cell text and value attributes after only Txt::utf8Encode() with no HTML escaping in VuePersonsImportExport.php. Attackers can craft a CSV cell containing an attribute-breakout payload that is rendered verbatim and executed in the browser of the administrator performing the import, leading to arbitrary script execution in the administrative context.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge the shared-calendar iCal share token by deriving md5Id() from predictable fields such as object creation time, which is self-disclosed through autorDate and the iCal CREATED field. Attackers can compute the creation minute and forge the md5Id token to access and read a shared calendar's iCal feed without authorization.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability in which the isAutor() function in MdlObject.php grants accessRight=3 based solely on object authorship without verifying the user still belongs to the object's space. Attackers who were previously members and authored objects can retain unauthorized read access to space objects even after being removed from the space, leading to persistent information disclosure.

A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability in the Audigy Rx driver’s Emupia2k.sys file could allow a local attacker with low privilege access to gain higher privileges, such as administrator rights.

A kernel pool buffer overflow vulnerability in the
ct0531fl.sys file of the Creative WDM Audio Driver (64-bit), Sound Blaster Audigy 4
      and Sound Blaster Audigy 5/Rx could allow a local
attacker with low privilege access to cause a denial of service.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5 and 1.5.1, a single unauthenticated BACnet/IP UDP datagram (port 47808) triggers an out-of-bounds read in xy_color_decode() (src/bacnet/lighting.c), reachable pre-authentication through two default-registered service handlers: the UnconfirmedRequest WriteGroup service (0x0A) and Confirmed WriteProperty on a BACnetXYColor-typed property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
