This issue affects Open Blue Companion Android App: before R2.22.0.

A local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability in Pebble’s installers could allow a local attacker with low privilege access to place a malicious Dynamic Link Library (DLL) where a privileged executable file will load it.

Hubleys is a dashboard for self-hosted services. Prior to version 0.5.2, any authenticated (non-admin) Hubleys user can upload a file with an arbitrary extension as their dashboard "background image," and the server will later serve that file back with a Content-Type derived straight from the attacker's chosen extension - so uploading an .html file gets it served as text/html. Because the endpoint that serves it returns a manually-constructed response rather than going through SvelteKit's normal page-rendering pipeline, the app's configured Content-Security-Policy never gets attached to it either, so a script embedded in the upload runs unrestricted. This issue has been patched in version 0.5.2.

bit-vec is a compact vector of bits. Prior to version 0.10.0, there is undefined behavior if a user performs deserialize from an untrusted source and unsafe get_unchecked. A user of this library may be impacted by incorrect behavior if they perform deserialize from an untrusted source and run operations on the deserialized BitVec. This issue has been patched in version 0.10.0.

PolicyPress is a compliance policy management tool for small and mid-size teams. Prior to version 1.4.1, sensitive content is disclosed via CSS-only web redaction and insecure starter workflow defaults. This issue has been patched in version 1.4.1.

Budget Board is an app for tracking monthly spending and working towards financial goals. Prior to version 3.6.2, Budget Board's OIDC login flow finds and signs into an existing local account purely by matching the email address asserted in the identity provider's token - it never checks the standard email_verified claim. If the configured OIDC provider ever allows a user to register or display an email address without proving they own it , an attacker can register there using a victim's email and get signed into the victim's existing Budget Board account - including all their linked bank data. This issue has been patched in version 3.6.2.

Hugo Blog is a tech blog site. In commit 744ca15 and prior, the AI assistant proxy exposes three HTTP endpoints (POST /api/blog-assistant, POST /api/blog-search-embedding, POST /api/blog-search-rerank) without any authentication check. When deployed following the documented Nginx reverse-proxy setup, any unauthenticated remote attacker can send arbitrary requests that the proxy forwards to the upstream LLM/embedding/rerank API using the operator's server-side API key (OPENAI_API_KEY / AI_SEARCH_API_KEY). This enables unlimited quota consumption, cost exhaustion, and potential service unavailability for the operator. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

A flaw was found in AWX. The debug API endpoints (/api/debug/task_manager/, /api/debug/dependency_manager/, /api/debug/workflow_manager/) are registered unconditionally in the URL configuration and use AllowAny permission class with _ignore_model_permissions=True. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to repeatedly invoke scheduler operations that acquire database advisory locks and open transactions, potentially leading to resource exhaustion and degraded service availability.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows an authenticated Webservice API key holder to read and modify customer records belonging to any shop in a multi-shop installation. Attackers can exploit the missing record-level shop ownership check in shopHasRight() and saveEntityFromXml() to read sensitive customer data such as password hashes and secure keys, and change a customer's email and password via create, update, and delete requests, resulting in account takeover.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains an authorization flaw in the Webservice API that allows an attacker holding a key restricted to one shop to act on data of every shop by submitting requests with id_shop=all or id_shop_group=N, which expand the shop context without validating the key's actual shop associations and cause shopHasRight() to evaluate the expanded set as a disjunction. Attackers can exploit this flaw via classes/webservice/WebserviceRequest.php to read, modify, or delete data belonging to shops they are not authorized for, including full customer records such as email addresses, secure_key, and password hashes across the installation.

TrueConf Server contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthorized attacker with network access via port 4307/TCP to execute an arbitrary script.

TrueConf Server contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow an unauthorized remote attacker with network access via port 4307/TCP to use a specially crafted script to break out of the isolated environment and execute arbitrary code on the host system.

Metabase contains a SQL Injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to inject arbitrary SQL into the Metabase application database, which can give them administrator access to the instance. From there, the attacker could change the application configuration, steal stored credentials for the connected databases, read any data accessible through those connections, and export data.

Apache Shiro is vulnerable to session fixation when a user is authenticated via the "Remember me" functionality. In affected versions, when a subject is restored from a "Remember me" cookie, the existing session is not invalidated, nor is a new session created with a new ID.
Additionally, session IDs were accepted from the request URL even when session ID URL rewriting was disabled.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when RememberMe functionality is enabled.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by invalidating the existing session and creating a new session with a new ID when a subject is restored from a "Remember me" cookie, and by ignoring session IDs in the URL when URL rewriting is disabled.

Authorization annotations, such as @RequiresRoles and @RequiresPermissions, are not always enforced in some class or interface hierarchies.
Annotations declared on an interface were not enforced when using the shiro-guice, shiro-aspectj, shiro-cdi or shiro-jakarta-ee modules.
In addition, annotations declared on a class or a superclass were not always enforced when using shiro-guice or shiro-aspectj, allowing an unauthorized caller to invoke methods that should be protected.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, with impact depending on module and where annotations are declared.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue. The annotation closest to the invoked method now takes precedence.
Alternatively, declare authorization annotations directly on each protected implementing method.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an insufficient verification of data authenticity vulnerability in the mt_wifi Smart Mesh Technology (SMT) onboarding, which protects messages only with an AES-CBC key derived from public values and a CRC32 check. Adjacent unauthenticated attackers can forge SMT messages in Probe Request vendor IEs carrying an attacker-chosen SSID and pre-shared key, forcing unpaired devices to join attacker-controlled access points.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to run root commands by advertising a rogue automesh controller over mDNS. Attackers on the upstream Ethernet segment can advertise _cudycmagent._tcp records pointing to a malicious MQTT broker, then send commands encrypted with a fixed AES key that router/batchcmd.lua executes as root.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in an obuspa getter for the TR-098 WLANConfiguration KeyPassphrase parameter, which copies the stored value with strcpy() into a 4,096-byte stack buffer without a length check. A malicious or compromised ACS can set a 5,000-byte passphrase via SetParameterValues, and a later read of the parameter overflows the buffer and crashes obuspa, causing denial of service.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows a malicious or compromised ACS to inject curl options through unfiltered Username and Password values in the easycwmpd Upload handler. Attackers can embed whitespace to add options like -o and --url to the root-run curl command, writing attacker-controlled HTTP responses to arbitrary files on the device.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by storing a malicious WireGuard private key. Attackers can save a private_key containing $() shell substitution and call the vpn.export_conf method on the /cgi-bin/luci/rpc/app JSON-RPC endpoint, which passes the key to a wg pubkey shell command.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability in luci/model/cbi/vpn/openvpn/client.lua, which embeds the shellquote()-quoted remote host token of an uploaded OpenVPN configuration inside an already single-quoted sed program run by os.execute(), so the nested quotes terminate the outer quote. Authenticated administrators can upload an .ovpn file whose remote host token contains a semicolon to execute arbitrary commands as root.

An OS Command Injection vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

Improper handling of highly compressed data (data amplification) vulnerability in Fileorbis Bilişim Hizmetleri Ticaret Anonim Şirketi FileOrbis NextGen FileServer allows Sustained Client Engagement.

This issue affects FileOrbis NextGen FileServer: before 12.7.
IBM DataStage on Cloud Pak for Data 5.4.0.0 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to a server-side request forgery vulnerability.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization-bypass vulnerability. A low-privileged attacker could exploit it, potentially leading to elevation of privilege to administrator.
Dell PowerStore contains a content-injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to display misleading text on the genuine login page for phishing.
Dell PowerStore contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability to reach internal network services from the appliance.
Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to arbitrary root command execution on the appliance.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization bypass vulnerability. An authenticated administrator could exploit this vulnerability to bypass multi-approver controls on critical operations.
JFrog Artifactory contains an improper authentication vulnerability that under default configuration can allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to obtain administrative privileges.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.0 to before 1.4.6, 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, and 1.6.0 to before 1.6.1, the BACnet MS/TP receive path decodes COBS frames into an output pointer inside the same fixed input buffer, but passes the full input-buffer size as the decode capacity. A long valid COBS payload can therefore write past the end of the actual remaining buffer. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.1, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.

VITEC EZ TV Platform Server before 8.5.0 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the upload handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to upload arbitrary files by supplying a target filename in the X-FILENAME request header with no authentication or file type validation required. Attackers can upload a malicious ASPX file directly to the web-accessible uploads directory, where it is immediately executable by the web server, achieving remote code execution in the context of the web server process. Patches are available for versions 8.3.0, 8.3.1, 8.4.0, and 8.4.1. Users running releases prior to 8.3.0 should upgrade to 8.5.0+.

The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Successful exploitation requires the existence of at least one Peer-to-Peer campaign. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82663 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.5. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know or discover an existing campaign and team ID to modify the team's name, story, goal, access and notification settings, set its profile image URL, and upload WordPress-allowed media files as parentless attachments. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82568 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

An unrestricted upload of files with dangerous type vulnerability in the Microchip TimePictra platform allows functionality not properly constrained by access control lists, potentially resulting in remote code execution.

SonicWall SMA1000 Appliances contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to gain unauthorized access to sensitive functionality and perform unauthorized operations.

LibreOffice can open PDF files in Draw, where the PDF import converts each page into drawing objects that can be edited. Images in the PDF, including images with a transparency mask, are converted along the way. An out-of-bounds write existed when an image with a transparency mask was converted, because positions taken from a crafted image were not checked against the size of the image buffer. In fixed versions the image size is limited, and the position of each mask pixel is checked before it is written.

LibreOffice Base documents can bind macros to document events, such as opening or closing the document. The macro security setting decides whether macros that come with a document may run. Macros bound to the events of a Base document were run without the macro security setting being applied, so opening or converting a crafted database document could run a macro and, through it, any command. In fixed versions macros bound to the events of a Base document follow the macro security setting, as macros in other documents do.
Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway contain an improper restriction of operations within the bounds of a memory buffer vulnerability which could lead to denial of service.

Mattermost Desktop App versions <=6.3 6.0.3 6.3.2.0 fail to handle filesystem errors that can occur when finalizing certain file downloads, which allows a malicious or compromised server to cause a denial of service by crashing the entire desktop application via a specially crafted download Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00779

termux-sync is an open source tool for backing up and restoring a Termux environment across devices. Prior to 1.2.4, termux-sync restore uses the parent directory of the untrusted manifest.json files.*.source value as an extraction destination, and extract_archive calls tarfile.extract on archive members without enforcing a destination boundary. A victim who restores a malicious or tampered backup from local, shared, GitHub, or Google Drive storage can have files written anywhere the Termux user can write, including shell startup files or executable scripts that can lead to code execution when later used. The restore path also accepts unsafe backup_name values for temporary paths, and archive members are not constrained to the intended destination. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.4.

A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::PersonalAccessTokensController, where Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user resolves the target account using User.find(params[:user_id]) without applying the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_personal_access_tokens permission can therefore invoke POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/personal_access_tokens with another user’s ID and create a Personal Access Token on their behalf. The resulting plaintext token is returned in the API response, while PersonalAccessToken#check_permissions_after_save only validates create_personal_access_tokens on the token and does not enforce edit_users authorization on the target user. The attacker can then use the forged token to authenticate as the victim, potentially resulting in complete account takeover, including administrator accounts.

A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::MailNotificationsController, where authorization checks on user-specific mail-notification resources are insufficient. The GET /api/v2/users/:id/mail_notifications endpoint resolves the target account using User.find(params[:id]) without verifying that the authenticated user is authorized to access that user’s notification configuration. Additionally, the POST and PUT /api/v2/users/:user_id/mail_notifications paths call deny_access when the requester is unauthorized but fail to halt execution, allowing the request to continue and persist the unauthorized change despite a 403 response or subsequent DoubleRenderError. This can allow a user to disclose another user’s mail-notification configuration, including mail_query values, and, where write permissions apply, modify or create notification settings for another user.

A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::SshKeysController, where the target user is resolved through Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user using User.find(params[:user_id]) without enforcing the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_ssh_keys permission can exploit this authorization bypass by submitting POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/ssh_keys with another user’s ID and injecting their own public SSH key into the targeted account. The injected key is subsequently propagated to hosts provisioned by that user, potentially allowing the attacker to authenticate to and gain SSH access to the victim’s managed hosts.
Dell PowerStore contains a use of a weak cryptographic algorithm vulnerability that could allow an attacker with existing privileged access to the appliance to recover stored credentials.

Dell PowerStore contains an External Control of File Name or Path vulnerability. A remote authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to privilege escalation on the appliance.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization-bypass vulnerability that could lead to elevation of privilege to administrator.

LibreOffice Writer can save documents in DOCX format. A document can contain content controls whose values are bound to custom XML data, and that data is updated with the current values when the document is exported, including in a conversion run from the command line. Values taken from the document were not escaped where they were used, so a crafted document could write a file of its choosing anywhere the user can write when it was exported to DOCX. In fixed versions these values are written into the document directly, and the XSLT transformations LibreOffice runs can no longer write files or use the network.

When Apache Shiro is used with the Jakarta EE integration module, the automatic form saving feature weakens the security of a form that is resubmitted after login.
Cookies set by the application during the resubmission could lose their security attributes, such as `Secure` and `SameSite`.
In addition, the resubmitted form data and cookies could be sent to an untrusted host.
This issue affects Apache Shiro from 2.0.0-alpha through 3.0.1, only when using `shiro-jakarta-ee` integration module with form saving enabled (the default).

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which no longer replays the form over the network, and avoids this class of issues entirely.
Alternatively, you can set the `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-host` (String) and `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-port` (Integer) system properties to restrict the host and port that Shiro will connect to when resubmitting a form.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not remove script-capable XHTML and XML data URIs from stored CMS content. A CMS author can save such content, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views it. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not remove SVG data URIs from stored CMS content even though SVG documents can execute script. A CMS author can save such content, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views it. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, a CMS user who can edit records through a GridField detail form can send a direct save request that creates a new record even when the user does not have permission to create that record type. The server-side save path checks edit access but does not enforce the required create permission before persistence. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Dolibarr before 24.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the REST Documents API for the ticket module that allows authenticated API users to access ticket attachments belonging to other companies by omitting a company-scope check that is only applied via a session variable set during public ticket authentication, which REST API authentication never sets. Attackers with ticket read permission can enumerate predictable ticket identifiers and supply them to the documents endpoint or download path to retrieve sensitive attachments such as invoices and contracts belonging to other third parties.

A vulnerability in the GenericAdminAuthenticator component of Azul Payara Server and Azul Payara Micro allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to bypass JMX/RMI administrative access restrictions by spoofing the client host address. Successful exploitation can grant administrative access to the MBean server and lead to remote code execution. Azul Payara Micro is affected only when its JMX connector is enabled.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not normalize certain control bytes that browsers ignore when parsing URLs. A CMS author can place those bytes before a javascript: URL in stored content so the sanitiser misses the dangerous scheme, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views the content. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, a user with CMS_ACCESS_SecurityAdmin but without ADMIN can edit or reparent a group that grants ADMIN-equivalent permissions through an assigned role or a parent group, thereby escalating to full administrative privileges. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, a CMS user who can edit a record through a GridField detail form can submit a user-controlled ClassName value to change the record into an unrelated class without the create and edit permission checks required for that target class. This permits an unauthorized record type change outside the GridField's intended model hierarchy. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, PermissionCheckboxSetField accepts permission codes that the field did not offer and stores them without an allowlist, then renders permission codes without escaping them. A user with access to the Security section can save attacker-controlled content as a permission code, causing JavaScript to execute in the browser of another user who views the field. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. From 6.0.0 until 6.2.13, the writer option of i18nTextCollectorTask is passed to the dependency injector without validating that it names an allowed writer implementation. A crafted dev task URL can therefore instantiate arbitrary objects with attacker-controlled constructor arguments and execute code on the server. An administrator can be induced to run the task by following a link because the nested task did not require confirmation, and a site in dev mode exposes the path without authentication. CMS 5 is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.
IBM Security QRadar EDR 3.12 through 3.12.26 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper access control.
IBM Security QRadar EDR 3.12 through 3.12.26 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to bypass security restrictions due to improper rate limiting on TOTP verification.

HashiCorp Vault and Vault Enterprise are vulnerable to an issue in the integrated storage join process that may allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a new, uninitialized node to cause that node to send credentials from its server environment to an attacker-controlled server. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92735) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault's Login MFA feature did not consistently enforce the lifetime of pending two-phase login requests. This may allow a user who previously completed the first authentication factor to complete MFA and obtain a Vault token after the pending request should have expired, including after the user's primary credential has been rotated. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92738) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.26.

Vault's audit devices did not validate the contents of a configured audit log prefix and did not consistently enforce the server-level setting that restricts audit log prefixing. This may allow a privileged operator to inject content into audit logs, potentially leading to forged or misleading audit records. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93333) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not consistently apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to request paths that differ only by a trailing slash. This may allow an authenticated user who holds a broader delete permission on system configuration paths to disable a secrets engine, auth method, or audit device that a more specific deny rule was intended to protect. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93335) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Station Launcher App in 3DEXPERIENCE platform from Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2023x through Release 3DEXPERIENCE R2026x could lead to an unauthenticated remote code execution.

IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.11 is potentially vulnerable to denial of service due to uncontrolled regular expression complexity (CWE-400 / ReDoS). An authenticated user with tool-registration privileges can embed catastrophically backtracking regex patterns in a tool's JSON Schema `pattern` field; when ContextForge validates arguments against that schema, the validation call may consume unbounded CPU, potentially degrading gateway availability.

OS command injection in the TFTP provisioning module of Zenitel EdgeAudioClient before 9.6.3.0, and 10.x before 10.1.3.0, on VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root via a crafted DHCP option 66 (TFTP Server Name) value supplied by a rogue DHCP server on the same network segment. The DHCP-supplied value is passed to a shell without sanitization. Devices using DHCP, the default configuration, are affected on every boot and lease renewal.



The same injection is also reachable via the config_update_tftp_server and sw_update_tftp_server configuration fields by an attacker able to modify the device configuration.

Path traversal in the certificate upload endpoint (/api/certificate/upload) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to write arbitrary files as root via a crafted filename parameter in a multipart upload request when the type field is set to any value other than https_certificate. In that case, both path validation and certificate content validation are skipped.



This can be escalated to arbitrary code execution as root, for example by overwriting startup scripts or planting SSH keys.

Path traversal in the certificate.deleteCertificate JSON-RPC method (POST /api/rpc) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to delete arbitrary files as root via a relative path (../) in the file_name parameter.



This can be used to cause denial of service or render the device inoperable by removing critical system files, and to weaken device security by removing files such as firewall rules or certificate trust stores.

Time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability in TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Yazılım Teknolojileri Araştırma Enstitüsü Pardus Package Installer allows Leveraging Time-of-Check and Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) Race Conditions.

This issue affects Pardus Package Installer: from 0.7.0 before 0.7.1.

The pREST database REST API in Zenitel Connect firmware before 1.11.0 signs and verifies JWTs with the platform CA private key, which is stored on a data volume shared between containers, and sets the PostgreSQL session role from the unvalidated sub claim of each request while connected to the database as the "postgres" superuser, which allows local attackers who can read the platform CA private key from the container filesystem to execute database operations as the PostgreSQL superuser, including reading the master encryption key and password hashes, via a forged JWT with sub=postgres sent to the pREST API.

The host configuration watcher in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 applies a rsyslog configuration file written to a data volume that is shared with the hiatus application container, which allows local attackers with write access to the hiatus container filesystem to execute arbitrary OS commands as root on the host operating system via a crafted rsyslog configuration file.

OS command injection vulnerability in audio messages API in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary OS commands as root in the hiatus application container via filename parameter to the /api/system/audio_messages endpoint.

Poste Italiane Postecert FIRMAOK! 1.6.29 on Windows contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability caused by an uncontrolled OpenSSL search path, where launcher.exe and dependent executables such as updater.exe and tslupdater.exe load OpenSSL configuration and library files from a hardcoded, user-writable directory that does not exist by default. A low-privileged local attacker can create this missing directory and place malicious OpenSSL configuration or library files inside it, causing the application to load and execute attacker-controlled code with the privileges of the user running it, enabling horizontal or, when a higher-privileged user runs the application, vertical privilege escalation up to full system compromise.

Plex Media Server contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability which could allow an attacker using any X-Plex-Token value to include a full URL in the 'protocol' parameter and force the Plex server to POST to the attacker's chosen destination. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656.

Plex Media Server contains an improper neutralization of encoded URI schemes in a web page vulnerability that could allow an attacker to call other plugins' functions and supply their own parameters. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96655, and CVE-2026-96656.

Plex Media Server contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to request arbitrary internal or external addresses via the '/video/:/transcode/universal' path parameter. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, and CVE-2026-96656.

Plex Media Server contains an external control of file name or path vulnerability which can allow an admin user to write arbitrary files that may be executed on load. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, and CVE-2026-96655.

An Out-Of-Bounds Write due to missing input validation is possible in the autoprogramming interface of SpaceCom and Space Battery pack with WiFi which could lead to a denial of service of the affected communication device
An inclusion of web functionality from an untrusted source could allow remote code execution on SpaceCom
There exists an improper privilege management vulnerability that could cause privilege escalation at the SpaceCom and Space Battery pack SP with WiFi.
IBM Cyber Fraud 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 could allow a local attacker to bypass security restrictions due to a missing or misconfigured security context.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, and 1.6.1, the BACnet/SC message decoder walks the header-option list by following each option's MORE bit. Nothing rejects a list whose last option still has the MORE bit set, and the decode walk has no upper bound on how many options it processes. A single crafted BVLC-SC frame makes the walk advance one option past the end of the message and read message[message_len], one byte out of bounds. When the bytes after the message carry more MORE-set option markers, the walk keeps going: it runs past the fixed 4-entry option array and writes decoded option fields out of bounds. On the server that decode array is the static global bsc_dm, so the out-of-bounds write lands in adjacent BSS. Both faults are reachable before authentication, from the first frame a peer sends on a BACnet/SC connection, and the bytes that follow the message are the same peer's prior-frame data. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.

LibreOffice checks the digital signatures of a PDF document when the document is opened, and shows whether each signature is valid. An out-of-bounds write existed when a signature was checked, because the parts of the file that a crafted signature claims to cover were not checked against the size of the file. In fixed versions a signature that claims to cover anything outside the file is reported as not valid.

LibreOffice Calc can open spreadsheets in the DIF format, and text files such as CSV in the UTF-16 encoding. Both are read one line at a time. An out-of-bounds read existed when a line of a crafted file was read, because the length of the line could be miscalculated, so memory beyond the line could be copied into the imported document. In fixed versions each line is read up to its limit and no further.

LibreOffice Base documents can hold an embedded HSQLDB database. When the experimental features option is enabled, LibreOffice offers to migrate such a database to the embedded Firebird engine when the document is opened. A heap buffer overflow existed when binary values were copied during the migration, because a value could be longer than the space set aside for its column. In fixed versions that space is enlarged whenever a value is longer than its column.

LibreOffice can import documents in the HWP format, including pictures that link to an external file. An out-of-bounds read existed when the link target of a crafted picture was read, so memory past the picture data could end up in the converted document. In fixed versions the link target is taken only from the picture data.
IBM Cyber Fraud 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 could allow an unauthorized user to inject data into log messages due to improper neutralization of special elements when written to log files.

IBM Cyber Fraud 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF

ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id() supersedes a prior open that has the
same AppInstanceId. It reaches that open's session through opinfo->sess.
This pointer is not refcounted.

Session teardown detaches durable handles before it frees the session.
It does not detach a non-durable open. That open still points at the
session through opinfo->sess after the session is freed. Another session
can supersede the open at the same time. The supersede then takes a
write lock through the stale pointer, in the freed session's file table.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
  Call Trace:
   _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
   ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id+0xd9/0x670 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x3e10/0xd910 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 212:
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0x38d/0x480 [ksmbd]

Fix this by looking the session up by opinfo->session_id. The lookup
returns a reference, as smb2_break_collect_channels() does. Recheck that
opinfo->sess still points at it before using it.

Do the lookup without m_lock held. destroy_previous_session() takes
m_lock under the session table lock, and taking them in the other order
here would deadlock.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the
reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry.
If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to
remove the volatile id.

Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before
either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops
its references first, the other request makes the final put through
ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first
session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed
memory.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 1030:
   __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd]

Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file
lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not
one made by another holder.

Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path,
before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the
request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which
holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup
is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow

smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() uses the MAX_CIFS_SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE
(448-byte) buffer for a single SMB2_CREATE response. That buffer also
holds a 4-byte length field, which only leaves 444 bytes for the SMB2
body.

The AAPL response made this buffer too small. After 8f1b796ff113, a
request with AAPL response contexts may need at least 456 bytes. In
the 456-byte case, create_aapl_rsp_buf() is appended last, clears 128
bytes, and writes 12 bytes past the allocation.

KASAN reports:

    BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    Write of size 128 at addr ffff88800370954c by task kworker/0:0/9
    ...
    create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    smb2_open+0x58f9/0xef10
    ...
    smb2_allocate_rsp_buf+0x19d/0x370
    ...
    The buggy address is located 332 bytes inside of
     allocated 448-byte region [ffff888003709400, ffff8880037095c0)

Reserve enough space for any fixed CREATE response KSMBD can build.
Store the required allocation size in the per-dialect values table.
This keeps the small buffer for other commands and avoids using the max
transaction buffer for every CREATE.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after
commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group
rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or
5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace)
on posix).

However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() ->
copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total),
and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes)
even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security
descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or
dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past
the end of the slab buffer.

Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of
id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fuse: don't BUG when the copy buffer is exhausted

fuse_copy_fill() hits BUG_ON(!err) once the iterator backing the copy
runs out of pages.  Over io-uring the amount copied is not bounded by the
payload buffer the server registered, so an unprivileged user can drain
the iterator and panic the host - mount a FUSE filesystem with small
payload buffers, then setxattr() a larger value:

  kernel BUG at fs/fuse/dev.c:1064!
  Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 148 Comm: exploit Not tainted 7.3.0-rc1 #2
  RIP: 0010:fuse_copy_fill (fs/fuse/dev.c:1033)
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   fuse_copy_args (fs/fuse/dev.c:1354 fs/fuse/dev.c:1380)
   fuse_uring_args_to_ring (fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:891)
   fuse_uring_prepare_send (fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:940 fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:1057)
   fuse_uring_send_in_task (fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:1745)
   tctx_task_work_run (io_uring/tw.c:96)
   tctx_task_work (io_uring/tw.c:133)
   task_work_run (kernel/task_work.c:233)
   io_run_task_work (io_uring/tw.h:84)
   io_cqring_wait (io_uring/wait.c:278)
   __do_sys_io_uring_enter (io_uring/io_uring.c:2676)
   do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61)
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121)

The reply path can drain it the same way, via the server-supplied
payload_sz in fuse_uring_copy_from_ring().

Return -EIO instead.  All three fuse_copy_fill() callers already
propagate the error.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nft_fwd_netdev: use recursion counter in neigh egress path

nft_fwd_neigh can be used in egress chains (NF_NETDEV_EGRESS). When the
forwarding rule targets the same device or two devices forward to each
other, neigh_xmit() triggers dev_queue_xmit() which re-enters

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len

of the reply buffer, instead of msg->front.iov_len, the number of bytes the
monitor sent.  mon_alloc_msg() routes every CEPH_MSG_MON_COMMAND_ACK to

received: uninitialized slab memory, stale bytes of an earlier message, or
bytes the peer planted by sending a reply that lands in the same buffer and
is then rejected.  The read stays within the allocation, so KASAN does not
flag it.

ceph_monc_get_version() and ceph_monc_blocklist_add(); rbd hands it back
from write() on /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major, and rbd_get_client() passes

which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode.

span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt.  Reject it where the rank
space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease

parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only
checks that many bytes are present, without requiring struct_len to cover
sizeof(struct ceph_mds_reply_lease) (10 bytes).  A malicious MDS can
declare a shorter record and still get the pointer published: the
following *p += sizeof(**lease) overshoot is undone by *p = lend, so
nothing downstream rejects the reply.  ceph_fill_trace() ->
update_dentry_lease() then reads 10 bytes through that pointer on any
lookup on a mounted CephFS, running past the end of the message front.

Require the record to cover the structure, matching the sibling
parse_reply_info_dir().  A conforming MDS always encodes the full 10
bytes.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow

High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and
are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512.
The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c
("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states
that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means.

But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will
allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to
1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because
xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this.

As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the
driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not
device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()

When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct
smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed,
Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This
only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So
the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd.

    unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset);
    int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset;

    if (!dacl_offset ||
	(dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size))
	    goto out;

fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out,
because it is only valid for 32-bit builds.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

  nfsd_dispatch

list.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()

When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains
other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash
like:

 Oops: general protection fault
 KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access
 RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503)
 Call Trace:
  vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419)
  do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583)
  __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602)

This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return
value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through
udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being
treated as a folio pointer with obvious results.

Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either
0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.
